sentences.zh: 馬韶楚芝蘭韓顯符史序周克明劉翰王懷隱趙自化馮文智沙門洪蘊蘇澄隱丁少微趙自然

translations.literal: Ma Shao, Chu Zhilan, Han Xianfu, Shi Xu, Zhou Keming, Liu Han, Wang Huaiyin, Zhao Zihua, Feng Wenzhi, the monk Hongyun, Su Chengyin, Ding Shaowei, Zhao Ziran
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao, Chu Zhilan, Han Xianfu, Shi Xu, Zhou Keming, Liu Han, Wang Huaiyin, Zhao Zihua, Feng Wenzhi, the Buddhist monk Hongyun, Su Chengyin, Ding Shaowei, and Zhao Ziran

sentences.zh: 昔者少皞氏之衰，九黎亂德，家為巫史，神人淆焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when the line of Shaohao declined, the Jiuli disturbed virtue; every household had shamans and clerks, and the divine and human realms became confused.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, as the house of Shaohao waned, the Jiuli threw virtue into disorder; shamans and recorders filled every home, and the realms of spirits and men grew indistinguishable.

sentences.zh: 顓頊氏命南正重司天以屬神，北正黎司地以屬民，其患遂息。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu ordered Nan Zheng Chong to oversee heaven and attach it to the divine, and Bei Zheng Li to oversee earth and attach it to the people, and the trouble then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu appointed Nan Zheng Chong to govern heaven on behalf of the spirits and Bei Zheng Li to govern earth on behalf of the people, and the disorder was stilled.

sentences.zh: 厥後三苗復棄典常，帝堯命羲、和修重、黎之職，絕地天通，其患又息。

translations.literal: Afterward the Three Miao again abandoned the constant norms; Emperor Yao ordered Xi and He to restore the offices of Chong and Li, severing earth from heaven and cutting off communication between them, and the trouble again ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Three Miao once more cast aside the established order; Emperor Yao charged Xi and He with reviving the posts of Chong and Li, sundering earth from heaven and breaking the link between them, and the trouble subsided again.

sentences.zh: 然而天有王相孤虛，地有燥濕高下，人事有吉凶悔吝、疾病劄瘥，聖人欲斯民趨安而避危，則巫醫不可廢也。

translations.literal: Yet heaven has its phases of prosperity and solitude, earth has dryness, moisture, elevation, and depth, and human affairs have fortune and misfortune, regret and difficulty, illness and ailments—the sage wishes the people to seek safety and avoid danger, so shamans and physicians cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven has its cycles of flourishing and decline, earth its dryness and damp, height and depth, and human life its fortune and misfortune, regret and affliction, sickness and recovery. Because the sage would have the people move toward safety and away from peril, shamans and physicians cannot be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 後世占候、測驗、厭禳、禬，至於兵家遁甲、風角、鳥占，與夫方士修煉、吐納、導引、黃白、房中，一切焄蒿妖誕之說，皆以巫醫為宗。

translations.literal: In later ages, observation of omens, testing and verification, exorcism and calamity-averting rites, down to military strategists' dunjia, wind-angle divination, and bird augury, and Daoist adepts' cultivation, breath regulation, guided exercise, gold-and-elixir work, and bedroom arts—all those murky, vaporous, demonic fables take shamans and physicians as their root tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, prognostication and verification, exorcism and plague-averting rites, military dunjia, wind-angle and bird augury, and the adepts' cultivation, breath-work, guided movement, elixir-making, and bedroom arts—all those hazy, vaporous, and fantastic doctrines trace their lineage back to shamans and healers.

sentences.zh: 漢以來，司馬遷、劉歆又亟稱焉。

translations.literal: Since Han times, Sima Qian and Liu Xin again repeatedly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han, Sima Qian and Liu Xin have praised such arts again and again.

sentences.zh: 然而歷代之君臣，一惑於其言，害於而國，凶於而家，靡不有之。

translations.literal: Yet rulers and ministers of successive dynasties, once deluded by their words, have harmed their states and brought ruin to their houses—there has been no lack of such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yet time and again, when rulers and ministers have been beguiled by such talk, states have suffered and families have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 宋景德、宣和之世，可鑒乎哉！

translations.literal: The Jingde and Xuanhe reign periods of Song—are they not a lesson!
translations.idiomatic: The Jingde and Xuanhe reigns of Song—are they not warning enough?!

sentences.zh: 然則歷代方技何修而可以善其事乎？

translations.literal: Then by what cultivation can technical specialists through the ages properly perform their craft?
translations.idiomatic: By what discipline, then, can specialists in these arts through the ages truly excel at their calling?

sentences.zh: 「曰：「人而無恒，不可以作巫醫。」

translations.literal: It says: "If a man lacks constancy, he cannot practice as shaman or physician."
translations.idiomatic: As it is said: "Without steadfastness, a man cannot serve as shaman or physician."

sentences.zh: 漢嚴君平、唐孫思邈呂才言皆近道，孰得而少之哉。

translations.literal: The words of Han's Yan Junping and Tang's Sun Simiao and Lü Cai all approached the Way—who could slight them?
translations.idiomatic: The teachings of Yan Junping of Han and of Sun Simiao and Lü Cai of Tang all drew near the Way—who could belittle them.

sentences.zh: 宋舊史有《老釋》、《符瑞》二誌，又有《方技傳》，多言禨祥。

translations.literal: The old Song histories had the Treatises on Laozi-Buddhism and on Portents, and also had a Biography of Technical Specialists, mostly discussing omens and auspices.
translations.idiomatic: The former Song histories included treatises on Laozi and Buddhism and on portents, as well as a Biography of Technical Specialists, most of it devoted to omens and auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 今省二誌，存《方技傳》雲。

translations.literal: Now the two treatises are omitted, and only the Biography of Technical Specialists is retained.
translations.idiomatic: Here the two treatises are omitted, and only the Biography of Technical Specialists is kept.

sentences.zh: 趙修己，開封浚儀人，少精天文推步之學。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiuji was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng; in youth he mastered astronomy and calendrical computation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiuji, a native of Junyi in Kaifeng, mastered astronomy and calendrical calculation while still young.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，李守真掌禁軍，領滑州節制，表為司戶參軍，留門下。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Later Jin, Li Shouzhen commanded the palace guards and held the military governorship of Huazhou; he recommended Xiuji as registrar of the revenue bureau and retained him at his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu reign of Later Jin, Li Shouzhen, who commanded the palace guards and held Huazhou as his military district, recommended Xiuji as revenue registrar and kept him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 守真每出征，修己必從，軍中占候多中。

translations.literal: Whenever Shouzhen went on campaign, Xiuji always accompanied him, and his prognostications in the army often proved correct.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shouzhen took the field, Xiuji went with him, and his military prognostications proved accurate again and again.

sentences.zh: 奏試大理評事，賜緋。

translations.literal: He was nominated for trial appointment as Dali reviewer and was granted scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for trial appointment as a Dali reviewer and was granted scarlet official robes.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，守真鎮蒲津，陰懷異志，修己屢以禍福諭之，不聽，遂辭疾歸鄉里。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou period of Later Han, Shouzhen was posted at Pu Ferry and harbored rebellious intentions in secret; Xiuji repeatedly used portents to admonish him, but Shouzhen would not listen, so Xiuji pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianyou era of Later Han, while Shouzhen held Pu Ferry and secretly nursed rebellious designs, Xiuji warned him repeatedly with omens of fortune and disaster, but Shouzhen would not heed him, so Xiuji pleaded illness and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 明年，守真果叛，幕吏多伏誅，獨修己得免。

translations.literal: The following year Shouzhen did rebel; many staff members were executed, but Xiuji alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shouzhen did rebel; many of his staff were put to death, but Xiuji alone escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其能，召為翰林天文。

translations.literal: The court, knowing his ability, summoned him as Hanlin astronomer.
translations.idiomatic: The court, recognizing his talent, summoned him to serve as Hanlin astronomer.

sentences.zh: 周祖嘗與處納同事漢祖，雅相厚善，及自鄴舉兵入汴，遽命訪求處訥，得之甚喜，因問以劉氏祚短事。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder had once served alongside the Han founder with Chune, between whom there was deep mutual regard; when he raised troops from Ye and entered Bian, he urgently ordered a search for Chune, and on finding him was greatly pleased, and therefore asked him about the brevity of the Liu dynasty's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder had once served the Han founder together with Wang Chune, and the two were on excellent terms. When he raised his army from Ye and entered Bian, he urgently ordered Chune sought out; on finding him he was overjoyed and asked why the Liu house's fortune would be brief.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「人君未得位，嘗務寬大；

translations.literal: He replied: "Before a ruler gains the throne, he always strives to be magnanimous;
translations.idiomatic: Chune answered: "Before a ruler gains the throne, he is always eager to show magnanimity;

sentences.zh: 既得位，即思復仇。

translations.literal: once he has gained it, he at once thinks of revenge.
translations.idiomatic: but once he has it, he turns at once to revenge.

sentences.zh: 漢氏據中土，承正統，以曆數推之，其大祀猶永。

translations.literal: The Han house holds the central lands and inherits the orthodox succession; by the reckoning of dynastic cycles, its great sacrifices should still be long-lasting.
translations.idiomatic: The Han hold the central realm and the orthodox succession; by the reckoning of dynastic cycles, their great rites ought still to endure.

sentences.zh: 第以高祖得位之後，多報仇殺人及夷人之族，結怨天下，所以運祚不長。」

translations.literal: Only after Gaozu took the throne he often avenged himself by killing people and exterminating clans, earning the hatred of the whole world—hence his fortune did not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Gaozu took the throne he killed widely in vengeance and exterminated whole clans, earning the hatred of all under heaven—hence the dynasty's fortune could not last.

sentences.zh: 周祖蹶然太息。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder started convulsively and sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder started as if struck and sighed deeply.

sentences.zh: 適發兵圍漢大臣蘇逢吉、劉銖等家，待旦將行孥戮，遽命止之。

translations.literal: Just then troops had been sent to surround the homes of Han ministers Su Fengji, Liu Zhu, and others, waiting until dawn to exterminate their families; he urgently ordered this stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At that very moment troops had been sent to surround the homes of Han ministers Su Fengji, Liu Zhu, and others, waiting for dawn to slaughter their families to the last; he urgently ordered the operation halted.

sentences.zh: 逢吉已自殺，止誅劉銖，餘悉全活。

translations.literal: Fengji had already killed himself; only Liu Zhu was executed, and all the rest were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji had already taken his own life; only Liu Zhu was executed, and all the rest were spared.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，遷司天少監。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun period he was promoted to Vice Director of the Astronomical Service.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun he was promoted to Vice Director of the Astronomical Service.

sentences.zh: 世宗以舊曆差舛，俾處訥詳定。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong found the old calendar erroneous and had Chune examine and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong found the old calendar in error and ordered Chune to revise it in detail.

sentences.zh: 曆成未上，會樞密使王樸作《欽天曆》以獻，頗為精密，處訥私謂樸曰：「此曆且可用，不久即差矣。」

translations.literal: When the calendar was finished but not yet submitted, the Privy Councilor Wang Pu produced the Qintian Calendar and presented it—it was quite precise; Chune privately told Pu, "This calendar can be used for now, but before long it will drift."
translations.idiomatic: Before Chune's calendar could be submitted, Privy Councilor Wang Pu presented the Qintian Calendar, which was quite precise. Chune told Pu privately, "This calendar will serve for the moment, but before long it will go wrong."

sentences.zh: 因指以示樸，樸深然之。

translations.literal: He pointed to show Pu why, and Pu deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed out the reasons to Pu, who was fully convinced.

sentences.zh: 至建隆二年，以《欽天曆》謬誤，詔處訥別造新曆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, because the Qintian Calendar was mistaken, an edict ordered Chune to compile a new calendar separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, because the Qintian Calendar was found erroneous, an edict ordered Chune to compile a new calendar on his own.

sentences.zh: 經三年而成，為六卷，太祖自製序，命為《應天曆》。

translations.literal: After three years it was finished, in six fascicles; Taizu himself wrote the preface and named it the Yingtian Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After three years' work it was finished in six fascicles; Taizu wrote the preface himself and named it the Yingtian Calendar.

sentences.zh: 處訥又以漏刻無準，重定水秤及候中星、分五鼓時刻。

translations.literal: Chune also found the clepsydra and night-watches inaccurate and redetermined the water balance, observation of culmination stars, and division of the five night-watch periods.
translations.idiomatic: Chune also found the clepsydra and night-watches unreliable and redetermined the water balance, the observation of culmination stars, and the division of the five night-watch periods.

sentences.zh: 俄遷少府少監。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，改司農少卿，並判司天事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was made Vice Minister of Agriculture while continuing to oversee astronomical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo era he was made Vice Minister of Agriculture while retaining charge of astronomical affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，又上新曆二十卷，拜司天監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again submitted a new calendar in twenty fascicles and was appointed Director of the Astronomical Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he submitted a new calendar in twenty fascicles and was appointed Director of the Astronomical Service.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: A little over a year later he died, at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子熙元。

translations.literal: His son was Xiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiyuan.

sentences.zh: 熙元，幼習父業，開寶中，補司天曆算。

translations.literal: Xiyuan studied his father's profession from childhood; in the Kaibao period he was appointed to calendar computation in the Astronomical Service.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan studied his father's craft from childhood; during Kaibao he was appointed to calendrical computation in the Astronomical Service.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改監丞，累遷太子洗馬兼春官正，加殿中丞，景德中，同判監事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was made supervisory commissioner, eventually rising to Groom-in-Waiting of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Director of the Spring Office, then added as Palace Administration Commissioner; in the Jingde period he served as co-administrator of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duan Gong he became a supervisory commissioner, rose through Groom-in-Waiting of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Director of the Spring Office to Palace Administration Commissioner, and in the Jingde era served as co-administrator of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 東封，隨經度製置使詣祠所。

translations.literal: During the eastern Fengshan rite he accompanied the longitude commissioner to the sacrificial site.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern Fengshan rite he accompanied the commissioner for longitudinal measurement to the sacrificial site.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，授權知司天少監。

translations.literal: When the rite was completed he was given acting authority as Vice Director of the Astronomical Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished he was granted acting authority as Vice Director of the Astronomical Service.

sentences.zh: 祠汾陰，真拜少監。

translations.literal: At the Fengyin sacrifice to Mount Fen he was formally appointed Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice to Mount Fen at the Fen River he was formally appointed Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 奉詔於後苑纘陰陽事十卷上之，真宗為製序，賜名《靈台秘要》，及作詩紀之。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled ten fascicles on yin-yang affairs in the rear garden and submitted them; Zhenzong wrote the preface, granting the title Secret Essentials of the Spirit Terrace, and also composed a poem to commemorate it.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he compiled ten fascicles on yin-yang matters in the rear garden and presented them; Zhenzong wrote the preface, gave the work the title Secret Essentials of the Spirit Terrace, and composed a poem to commemorate it.

sentences.zh: 初，上所修《儀天曆》，秋官正趙昭益言其二年後必差，又熒惑度數稍謬，後果驗。

translations.literal: Earlier the Yitian Calendar that he had compiled—the Autumn Office Director Zhao Zhaoyi said it would inevitably drift after two years, and that the degree positions of Mars were somewhat wrong—and later this was indeed verified.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, for the Yitian Calendar that Xiyuan had compiled, Autumn Office Director Zhao Zhaoyi said it would inevitably drift within two years and that the degree positions of Mars were slightly wrong—and this later proved true.

sentences.zh: 熙元頗伏其精一。

translations.literal: Xiyuan deeply respected Zhaoyi's precision.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan deeply admired Zhaoyi's precision.

sentences.zh: 上常對宰相言及曆算事，曰：「曆象，陰陽家流之大者，以推步天道，平秩人時為功。」

translations.literal: The emperor often spoke to his chief ministers about calendrical matters, saying: "The calendar and heavenly phenomena are the greatest achievements of the yin-yang specialist lineage—to pace the way of heaven and regulate the seasons for mankind is their merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often spoke to his chief ministers about calendrical affairs, saying: "Calendars and heavenly phenomena are the greatest achievement of the yin-yang specialists: their merit lies in pacing the way of heaven and setting the seasons in order for mankind."

sentences.zh: 且言：「昭益能專其業，人鮮及也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhaoyi can devote himself to this specialty—few can match him."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Zhaoyi can devote himself wholly to this craft—few can equal him."

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮成，以祗事之勤，授司天監。

translations.literal: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was completed, for his devoted service in rituals he was appointed Director of the Astronomical Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace was completed, he was appointed Director of the Astronomical Service for his devoted service in the rites.

sentences.zh: 坐擇日差謬，降為少監。

translations.literal: For errors in date-selection he was demoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: For errors in choosing auspicious dates he was demoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以目疾，改將作監，致仕。

translations.literal: Because of eye disease he was transferred to Director of Palace Construction and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because of eye trouble he was transferred to Director of Palace Construction and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi he died, at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianxi, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 苗訓，河中人，善天文占候之術。

translations.literal: Miao Xun was a man of Hedong, skilled in astronomy and omen observation.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Xun, a native of Hedong, was skilled in astronomy and the observation of omens.

sentences.zh: 仕周為殿前散員右第一直散指揮使。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as commander of the first right scatter guard of the palace front.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as commander of the first right scatter guard of the palace front.

sentences.zh: 顯德末，從太祖北征，訓視日上復有一日，久相摩蕩，指謂楚昭輔曰：「此天命也。」

translations.literal: At the end of Xiande, accompanying Taizu on the northern campaign, Xun saw that above the sun there was again a sun, rubbing against it for a long time; pointing, he told Chu Zhaofu: "This is the mandate of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiande, on Taizu's northern campaign, Xun saw a second sun above the sun, grinding against it for a long while; pointing, he told Chu Zhaofu, "This is Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 夕次陳橋，太祖為六師推戴，訓皆預白其事。

translations.literal: That evening they halted at Chenqiao; Taizu was elevated by the Six Armies—and Xun had informed him of all this beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the army halted at Chenqiao, where Taizu was raised up by the Six Armies—and Xun had foretold the whole affair to him in advance.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，擢為翰林天文，尋加銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication he was promoted to Hanlin astronomer, soon added Silver-Green Glory Grandee and acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After he received the abdication, Xun was promoted to Hanlin astronomer and soon given the titles Silver-Green Glory Grandee and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘卒。

translations.literal: He died in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 子守信。

translations.literal: His son was Shouxin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shouxin.

sentences.zh: 守信，少習父業，補司天曆算。

translations.literal: Shouxin studied his father's profession in youth and was appointed to calendar computation.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin studied his father's craft from youth and was appointed to calendrical computation.

sentences.zh: 尋授江安縣主簿，改司天台主簿，知算造。

translations.literal: Soon he was made magistrate of Jiang'an County, then chief clerk of the Astronomical Bureau, in charge of calendrical production.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made magistrate of Jiang'an County, then chief clerk of the Astronomical Bureau with charge of calendrical production.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，以《應天曆》小差，詔與冬官正吳昭素、主簿劉內真造新曆。

translations.literal: In Taiping Xingguo, because the Yingtian Calendar had small errors, an edict ordered him with Winter Office Director Wu Zhaosu and chief clerk Liu Neizhen to make a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo, because the Yingtian Calendar showed small errors, an edict ordered him, together with Winter Office Director Wu Zhaosu and chief clerk Liu Neizhen, to compile a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 及成，太宗命衛尉少卿元象宗與明律曆者同校定，賜號《乾元曆》，頗為精密，皆優賜束帛。

translations.literal: When it was finished, Taizong ordered Vice Minister of the Guard Yuan Xiangzong and those versed in calendars to examine it together; it was granted the name Qianyuan Calendar, was quite precise, and all were richly rewarded with silk.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, Taizong ordered Vice Minister of the Guard Yuan Xiangzong and experts in calendars to examine it jointly; it was granted the name Qianyuan Calendar, proved quite precise, and all received rich gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，遷冬官正。

translations.literal: In Yongxi he was promoted to Winter Office Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was promoted to Winter Office Director.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改太子洗馬、判司天監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was made Groom-in-Waiting and concurrent Administrator of the Astronomical Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duan Gong he was made Groom-in-Waiting of the Heir Apparent and concurrent administrator of the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，守信上言：「正月一日為一歲之首。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Shouxin submitted a memorial: "The first day of the first month is the head of the year.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, Shouxin submitted a memorial: "The first day of the first month is the beginning of the year.

sentences.zh: 每月八日，天帝下巡人世，察善惡。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of each month the Heavenly Emperor descends to tour the human world and inspect good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of each month the Heavenly Emperor descends to tour the human realm and inspect good and evil.

sentences.zh: 太歲日為歲星之精，人君之象。

translations.literal: The Tai Sui day is the essence of the Year Star, the image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Tai Sui day is the essence of the Year Star and the image of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 三元日，上元天官，中元地官，下元水官，各主錄人之善惡。

translations.literal: On the Three Primes days—the Upper Prime is the celestial official, the Middle Prime the earthly official, the Lower Prime the water official—each records people's good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: On the Three Primes days—the Upper Prime is the celestial official, the Middle Prime the earthly official, the Lower Prime the water official—each records the good and evil of mankind.

sentences.zh: 又春戊寅、夏甲午、秋戊申、冬甲子為天赦日，及上慶誕日，皆不可以斷極刑事。」

translations.literal: Also spring wuyin, summer jiawu, autumn wushen, and winter jiazi are Heaven's pardon days, as is the emperor's birthday—on none of these may capital punishment be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Spring wuyin, summer jiawu, autumn wushen, and winter jiazi are also Heaven's pardon days, as is the emperor's birthday—on none of these may capital punishment be imposed.

sentences.zh: 下有司議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉殿中丞、權少監事，立本品之下，俄賜金紫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Palace Administration Commissioner and acting Vice Director, ranked below his proper grade; soon he was granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Palace Administration Commissioner and acting Vice Director, ranked below his proper grade; soon he was granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，上以梁、雍宿兵，彌歲凶歉，心憂之，令宰相召守信問以天道咎證所在。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, because Liang and Yong had long-standing garrisons and famine had persisted for a year, the emperor was deeply troubled and ordered the chief ministers to summon Shouxin and ask where heaven's reproof and omens lay.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao, because Liang and Yong had long-standing garrisons and famine had lasted a full year, the emperor was deeply troubled and ordered the chief ministers to summon Shouxin and ask where heaven's reproof and omens lay.

sentences.zh: 守信奏曰：「臣仰瞻玄象，及推驗太一經歷宮分，其荊楚、吳越、交廣並皆安寧。

translations.literal: Shouxin memorialized: "Your subject, gazing up at the dark heavens and verifying by the Taiyi classic's passage through palace sectors, finds that Jingchu, Wu-Yue, Jiao-Guang are all at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin memorialized: "Your subject, gazing up at the dark heavens and verifying by the Taiyi classic's passage through the palace sectors, finds Jingchu, Wu-Yue, and Jiao-Guang all at peace.

sentences.zh: 自來五緯陵犯、彗星見及水神太一臨井鬼之間，屬秦、雍分及梁、益之地，民罹其災。

translations.literal: From past times the five planets in violation, the appearance of comets, and the Water Spirit Taiyi dwelling between Jing and Gui correspond to the Qin-Yong and Liang-Yi sectors—there the people suffer calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the five planets have trespassed, comets have appeared, or the Water Spirit Taiyi has dwelt between Jing and Gui, the sectors of Qin-Yong and Liang-Yi have suffered, and the people there have borne the calamity.

sentences.zh: 水神太一來歲入燕分，歲在房心，正當京都之地，自茲朝野有慶。」

translations.literal: The Water Spirit Taiyi next year enters the Yan sector; the year star is in Fang and Xin, directly over the capital region—from now on court and countryside will have cause for celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Water Spirit Taiyi will enter the Yan sector, and the year star will stand in Fang and Xin, directly over the capital—from this time forward court and countryside will have cause for rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 詔付史館。

translations.literal: An edict ordered this filed in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the memorial filed in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，真授少監。

translations.literal: The following year he was formally appointed Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was formally appointed Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he died, at age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Xianping, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 子舜卿，為國子博士。

translations.literal: His son Shunqing became Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shunqing became an Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 馬韶，趙州平棘人，習天文三式。

translations.literal: Ma Shao was a native of Pingji in Zhao prefecture, trained in the three styles of heaven astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao, a native of Pingji in Zhao prefecture, studied the three forms of heavenly astronomy.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，太宗以晉王尹京，申嚴私習天文之禁，韶素與太宗親吏程德玄善，德玄每戒韶不令及門。

translations.literal: In Kaibao, Taizong as Prince of Jin governed the capital and strictly banned private study of astronomy; Shao was on good terms with Taizong's intimate aide Cheng Dexuan, who often warned Shao not to come to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, when Taizong as Prince of Jin governed the capital, private study of astronomy was strictly forbidden; Shao was on good terms with Taizong's intimate aide Cheng Dexuan, who often warned Shao not to come to his gate.

sentences.zh: 九年冬十月十九日，既夕，韶忽造德玄，德玄恐甚，詰其所以來，韶曰：「明日乃晉王利見之辰，韶故以相告。」

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year, after evening, Shao suddenly visited Dexuan; Dexuan was greatly afraid and questioned why he had come; Shao said: "Tomorrow is the Prince of Jin's day of favorable vision—I therefore come to tell you."
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year, after nightfall, Shao suddenly called on Dexuan; Dexuan was terrified and demanded why he had come; Shao said, "Tomorrow is the Prince of Jin's day of favorable vision—I have come to tell you."

sentences.zh: 德玄惶駭，止韶一室，遽入白太宗。

translations.literal: Dexuan was terrified and confined Shao in one room, then hurried in to inform Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan, in alarm, locked Shao in a room and hurried in to inform Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗命德玄以人防守之，將聞於太祖。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Dexuan to have men guard him, intending to report to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered Dexuan to set men to guard Shao, intending to report the matter to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 及詰旦，太宗入謁，果受遺踐阼。

translations.literal: At dawn Taizong went to audience and indeed received the succession and ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Taizong went to audience and indeed received the succession and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 韶以赦獲免。

translations.literal: Shao was spared through the general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was spared through the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 逾月，起家為司天監主簿。

translations.literal: A month later he entered service as chief clerk of the Astronomical Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he entered service as chief clerk of the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，擢太僕寺丞，改秘書省著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and then Assistant in the Secretariat's works section.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and then made Assistant in the Secretariat's works section.

sentences.zh: 曆太子中允、秘書丞，出為平恩令。

translations.literal: He passed through Groom of the Heir Apparent, Secretariat Commissioner, and went out as magistrate of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Commissioner, then went out to serve as magistrate of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，復守舊任，與楚芝蘭同判司天監事，就遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He returned to court, again held his former post, together with Chu Zhilan concurrently administered Astronomical Directorate affairs, and was then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court, resumed his former duties, and together with Chu Zhilan served as concurrent administrator of Astronomical Directorate affairs before being promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，坐事，出為博興令，移長山令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, because of an offense he was sent out as magistrate of Boxing and then transferred to magistrate of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was punished for an offense, demoted to magistrate of Boxing, and later transferred to magistrate of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸鄉里，卒於家。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to his home district and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term of office ended he returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 楚芝蘭，汝州襄城人，初習《三禮》，忽自言遇有道之士，教以符天、六壬、遁甲之術。

translations.literal: Chu Zhilan was a native of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou; he first studied the "Three Rites," then suddenly said he had met a man of the Way who taught him the arts of Futian, Liuren, and Dunjia.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhilan, a native of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou, had first studied the Three Rites when he suddenly claimed to have met a man of the Way who taught him Futian, Liuren, and Dunjia divination.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷博求方技，詣闕自薦，得錄為學生。

translations.literal: When the court broadly sought technical specialists, he went to the capital to recommend himself and was enrolled as a student.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was broadly recruiting specialists in the technical arts, he went to the capital to recommend himself and was enrolled as a student.

sentences.zh: 以占候有據，擢為翰林天文。

translations.literal: Because his prognostications had a reliable basis, he was promoted to Hanlin Astronomer.
translations.idiomatic: Because his astrological prognostications proved reliable, he was promoted to Hanlin Astronomer.

sentences.zh: 授樂源縣主簿，遷司天春官正、判司天監事。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of Leyuan County, then promoted to Spring Office Director of the Astronomical Directorate and concurrent administrator of directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Leyuan County, then promoted to Spring Office Director of the Astronomical Directorate and concurrent administrator of directorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 占者言五福太一臨吳分，當於蘇州建太一祠。

translations.literal: Prognosticators said the Five Blessings Grand Unity was over the Wu asterism, and a Grand Unity shrine should be built at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prognosticators reported that the Five Blessings Grand Unity deity was positioned over the Wu asterism and that a Grand Unity shrine should be built at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 芝蘭獨上言：「京師帝王之都，百神所集。

translations.literal: Zhilan alone memorialized: "The capital is the city of emperors, where the hundred spirits gather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilan alone submitted a memorial: "The capital is the city of emperors, where all the spirits assemble.

sentences.zh: 且今京城東南一舍地名蘇村，若於此為五福太一建宮，萬乘可以親謁，有司便於祗事，何為遠趨江外，以蘇台為吳分乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, one li southeast of the capital today is a place called Sucun; if a palace for the Five Blessings Grand Unity is built here, the ten-thousand-chariot ruler can personally visit, and the officials can conveniently perform reverent service—why go far beyond the river and treat Sutai as the Wu asterism?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a place called Sucun lies just one li southeast of the capital; if a palace to the Five Blessings Grand Unity were built there, the emperor could visit in person and the officials could conveniently perform the rites—so why travel far beyond the Yangzi and treat Suzhou as the Wu asterism?

sentences.zh: 輿論不能奪，遂從其議，仍令同定本宮四時祭祀儀及醮法。

translations.literal: Public opinion could not overturn him, so they followed his proposal and still ordered him to help fix the four-season sacrificial rites and jiao ritual methods for that palace.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion could not overturn his view, so the court adopted his proposal and also ordered him to help establish the four-season sacrificial rites and jiao rituals for the new palace.

sentences.zh: 宮成，特遷尚書工部員外郎，賜五品服。

translations.literal: When the palace was completed, he was specially promoted to Secretary in the Ministry of Works and granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace was completed, he received a special promotion to Secretary in the Ministry of Works and was granted fifth-rank court robes.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，與馬韶同判監，俱坐事，芝蘭出為遂平令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, together with Ma Shao he concurrently administered the directorate; both were punished for offenses, and Zhilan was sent out as magistrate of Suiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunhua era he served with Ma Shao as concurrent administrator of the directorate; both were punished for offenses, and Zhilan was demoted to magistrate of Suiping.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 錄其子繼芳為城父縣主簿。

translations.literal: His son Jifang was enrolled as chief clerk of Chenggu County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jifang was granted appointment as chief clerk of Chenggu County.

sentences.zh: 韓顯符，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Han Xianfu—of what place he was is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xianfu was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 少習三式，善察視辰象，補司天監生，遷靈台郎，累加司天冬官正。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Three Styles, was skilled at observing the stars, was appointed a student of the Astronomical Directorate, was promoted to Spirit Platform Gentleman, and was repeatedly promoted to Winter Office Director of the Astronomical Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied the Three Styles and was skilled at observing the heavens; he entered service as a student of the Astronomical Directorate, rose to Spirit Platform Gentleman, and was eventually promoted to Winter Office Director of the Astronomical Directorate.

sentences.zh: 顯符專渾天之學，淳化初，表請造銅渾儀、候儀。

translations.literal: Xianfu specialized in armillary-sphere learning; at the beginning of Chunhua he memorialized requesting the casting of a bronze armillary sphere and observational instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu specialized in armillary-sphere astronomy, and at the beginning of the Chunhua era he submitted a memorial requesting the casting of a bronze armillary sphere and observational instruments.

sentences.zh: 詔給用度，俾顯符規度，擇匠鑄之。

translations.literal: An edict granted expenses and had Xianfu design and measure, select craftsmen, and cast them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the necessary funds and ordered Xianfu to design the instruments, take measurements, select craftsmen, and cast them.

sentences.zh: 至道元年渾儀成，於司天監築台置之，賜顯符雜彩五十匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao the armillary sphere was completed; a platform was built at the Astronomical Directorate to place it, and Xianfu was granted fifty bolts of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao the armillary sphere was completed; a platform was built at the Astronomical Directorate to house it, and Xianfu was granted fifty bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 顯符上其《法要》十卷，序之云：

translations.literal: Xianfu submitted his ten-juan "Essential Methods," and in the preface said:
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu submitted his ten-juan work "Essential Methods," writing in the preface:

sentences.zh: 自伏羲甲寅年至皇朝大中祥符三年庚戌歲，積三千八百九十七年。

translations.literal: From the jiayin year of Fuxi to the gengxu year of the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu in our dynasty, the accumulated span is three thousand eight hundred ninety-seven years.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiayin year of Fuxi to the gengxu year, the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu in our dynasty, the accumulated span is three thousand eight hundred ninety-seven years.

sentences.zh: 五帝之後訖今，明曆象之玄，知渾天之奧者，近十餘朝，考而論之，臻至妙者不過四五。

translations.literal: From after the Five Emperors until today, those who understood the mysteries of the calendar and asterisms and knew the profundities of the armillary sphere, in nearly ten-plus dynasties, examined and discussed—those reaching supreme excellence were no more than four or five.
translations.idiomatic: From the age after the Five Emperors down to the present, among the nearly dozen dynasties of men who understood the mysteries of calendrics and astronomy and grasped the profundities of the armillary sphere, no more than four or five ever reached true mastery.

sentences.zh: 自餘徒誇重於一日，不深圖於久要，致使天象無準，曆算漸差，占候不同，盈虛難定。

translations.literal: The rest merely boasted of weight for one day and did not deeply plan for long-term essentials, causing celestial phenomena to lack standards, calendar calculations gradually to diverge, prognostications to differ, and fullness and emptiness to be hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: The rest merely boasted of short-term success and gave no deep thought to long-term needs, with the result that celestial phenomena lost their standards, calendar calculations gradually drifted, prognostications disagreed, and waxing and waning could no longer be reliably determined.

sentences.zh: 陛下講求廢墜，爰造渾儀，漏刻星躔，曉然易辨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeks and restores what has fallen into ruin, and therefore made the armillary sphere; clepsydra graduations and star positions are clearly easy to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sought to revive what had fallen into ruin and has therefore had this armillary sphere made, so that clepsydra graduations and stellar positions are clear and easy to discern.

sentences.zh: 若人目窺於下，則銅管運於上，七曜之進退盈縮，眾星之次舍遠近，占逆順，明吉凶，然後修福俾順其度，省事以退其災，悉由斯器驗之。

translations.literal: If the human eye looks down below, then the bronze tubes move above; the seven luminaries' advance, retreat, expansion, and contraction, the myriad stars' stations near and far—examining compliance and reversal, clarifying auspiciousness and misfortune—then cultivating fortune to accord with their measures and reducing affairs to avert disaster: all are verified through this instrument.
translations.idiomatic: When the eye looks down below, the bronze tubes move above; the advance, retreat, expansion, and contraction of the seven luminaries and the stations near and far of the myriad stars can be examined for compliance or reversal and interpreted for good or ill fortune—so that merit may be cultivated to accord with their measures and affairs simplified to avert disaster—all verified through this instrument.

sentences.zh: 昔漢洛下閎修渾儀，測《太初曆》云：「後五百年必當重製。」

translations.literal: Formerly in Han, Luoxia Hong repaired the armillary sphere and, measuring the "Taichu Calendar," said: "After five hundred years it must be remade."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Han, Luoxia Hong repaired the armillary sphere and, while working on the Taichu Calendar, said, "After five hundred years it must be remade."

sentences.zh: 至唐李淳風，果合前契。

translations.literal: Reaching Tang's Li Chunfeng, it indeed matched the former covenant.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tang, when Li Chunfeng came, the prophecy indeed proved true.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 淳風又言前代渾儀得失之差，因令銅鑄。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng again spoke of the gains, losses, and differences of former generations' armillary spheres and therefore ordered them cast in bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng then explained the strengths and weaknesses of earlier armillary spheres and ordered a new one cast in bronze.

sentences.zh: 七年，太宗起凝暉閣於禁中，俾侍臣占驗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Taizong erected Ninghui Pavilion in the inner palace and had attendant ministers prognosticate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Taizong built Ninghui Pavilion within the inner palace and had his attendant ministers use it for astronomical observation and verification.

sentences.zh: 既在宮掖，人莫得見，後失其處所。

translations.literal: Since it was inside the palace women's quarters, people could not see it, and later its location was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Because it stood within the inner palace, ordinary people could not see it, and in time its location was lost.

sentences.zh: 玄宗命沙門一行修《大衍曆》，蓋以渾儀為證。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered the monk Yixing to revise the "Dayan Calendar," covering to use the armillary sphere as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered the monk Yixing to revise the Dayan Calendar, using the armillary sphere as verification.

sentences.zh: 又有梁令瓚造渾儀木式，一行謂其精密，思出古人，遂以銅鑄。

translations.literal: There was also Liang Lingzan, who made a wooden model armillary sphere; Yixing said it was precise and thought it surpassed the ancients, and therefore had it cast in bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Lingzan also made a wooden model armillary sphere; Yixing judged it precise and superior to the ancients, and so had it cast in bronze.

sentences.zh: 今文德殿鼓樓下有古本銅渾儀一，製極疏略，不可施用。

translations.literal: Now beneath the drum tower of Wende Hall there is one old bronze armillary sphere; its construction is extremely crude and cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Today beneath the drum tower of Wende Hall stands an old bronze armillary sphere whose construction is extremely crude and unusable.

sentences.zh: 且曆象之作，非渾儀無以考真偽；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the making of calendars and asterisms, without an armillary sphere there is no means to examine truth and falsehood;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in calendrical and astronomical work, without an armillary sphere there is no way to test what is true and what is false;

sentences.zh: 算造之士，非占驗不能究得失。

translations.literal: Scholars of calculation and construction, without prognostication and verification cannot investigate gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: and for those who calculate and construct calendars, without observation and verification they cannot determine what succeeds and what fails.

sentences.zh: 渾儀之成，則司天歲上細行曆。

translations.literal: When the armillary sphere is completed, then the Astronomical Directorate yearly submits the detailed ephemeris calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armillary sphere is completed, the Astronomical Directorate can submit a detailed annual ephemeris each year.

sentences.zh: 益可致其詳密。

translations.literal: This can further achieve its detailed precision.
translations.idiomatic: This can achieve still greater precision.

sentences.zh: 其制有九，事具《天文志》。

translations.literal: Its construction has nine parts; the matter is fully recorded in the "Astronomical Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: Its construction has nine parts, which are fully described in the Astronomical Treatise.

sentences.zh: 自是顯符專測驗渾儀，累加春官正，又轉太子洗馬。

translations.literal: From this Xianfu specialized in testing and verifying the armillary sphere, was repeatedly promoted to Spring Office Director, and was also transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xianfu devoted himself to testing and verifying the armillary sphere, rose to Spring Office Director, and was later transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，詔顯符擇監官或子孫可以授渾儀法者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered Xianfu to select directorate officials or descendants who could be taught the armillary-sphere methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu an edict ordered Xianfu to select directorate officials or descendants who could be taught the methods of the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 顯符言長子監生承矩善察躔度，次子保章正承規見知算造，又主簿杜貽範、保章正楊惟德皆可傳其學。

translations.literal: Xianfu said his eldest son, the student Chengju, was skilled at observing stellar motion; his second son, Baozhang Director Chenggui, was known for calculation and construction; and Chief Clerk Du Yifan and Baozhang Director Yang Weide could all transmit his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu reported that his eldest son, the student Chengju, was skilled at observing stellar motion; his second son Chenggui, a Baozhang Director, was known for calendrical calculation; and Chief Clerk Du Yifan and Baozhang Director Yang Weide were all capable of passing on his art.

sentences.zh: 詔顯符與貽範等參驗之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xianfu together with Yifan and the others jointly to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xianfu to verify the candidates together with Yifan and the others.

sentences.zh: 顯符後改殿中丞兼翰林天文。

translations.literal: Later Xianfu was changed to Palace Supervisory Commissioner, concurrently Hanlin Astronomer.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu was later made Palace Supervisory Commissioner with concurrent appointment as Hanlin Astronomer.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 又詔監丞丁文泰嗣其事焉。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Supervising Commissioner Ding Wentai to succeed his affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Supervising Commissioner Ding Wentai to succeed to his duties.

sentences.zh: 史序字正倫，京兆人。

translations.literal: Shi Xu, styled Zhenglun, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xu, styled Zhenglun, was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 善推步曆算，太平興國中，補司天學生。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calendrical calculation and star steps; in Taiping Xingguo he was appointed a student of the Astronomical Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in calendrical calculation and astronomical computation, he entered service as a student of the Astronomical Directorate during the Taiping Xingguo era.

sentences.zh: 太宗親較試，擢為主簿。

translations.literal: Taizong personally tested him and selected him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally examined him and selected him for appointment as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 稍遷監丞，賜緋魚，隸翰林天文院。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to supervising commissioner, granted the crimson fish pouch, and attached to the Hanlin Astronomical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to supervising commissioner, granted the crimson fish pouch, and assigned to the Hanlin Astronomical Academy.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，廷試中選者二十六人，而序為之首，命知算造，又知監事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, twenty-six people were selected in the palace examination, and Xu ranked first; he was ordered to manage calculation and construction and also to manage directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi twenty-six candidates passed the palace examination, with Xu ranking first; he was put in charge of calendrical calculation and also given responsibility for directorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，司天鄭昭宴言：「臣測金、火行度須有相犯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, Astronomical Directorate officer Zheng Zhaoyan said: "I calculate that the degrees of Metal and Fire in motion must have mutual violation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua, Zheng Zhaoyan of the Astronomical Directorate reported, "My calculations indicate that the degrees of Venus and Mars in motion ought to produce a mutual violation.

sentences.zh: 今驗之天，而火行漸南，金度漸北，有若相避，遂不相犯。」

translations.literal: Now verifying it in the sky, Fire in motion gradually moves south and Metal's degree gradually moves north, as if avoiding each other, and thus there is no mutual violation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I verify this against the sky, Mars gradually moves south while Venus moves north, as though avoiding each other, and so no violation occurs.

sentences.zh: 序又言：「木、火、金三星初夜在午，木在東，火在中，金最西，漸北行去火尺餘。

translations.literal: Xu also said: "Wood, Fire, and Metal three stars at first watch were in Wu; Wood was in the east, Fire in the middle, Metal westernmost, gradually moving north away from Fire by more than a chi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu added, "At first watch Jupiter, Mars, and Venus stood in the Wu sector: Jupiter in the east, Mars in the middle, and Venus farthest west, gradually moving north and drawing more than a chi away from Mars.

sentences.zh: 此國家欽崇天道，聖德所感也。」

translations.literal: This is the state reverently honoring Heaven's Way—the effect of sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the state reveres Heaven's Way and that sacred virtue has moved the heavens."

sentences.zh: 序後累遷夏官正、河西、環慶二路隨軍轉運、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Later Xu was repeatedly promoted to Summer Office Director, army transport commissioner following the armies on the Hexi and Huanqing circuits, and Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was later promoted to Summer Office Director, served as army transport commissioner with the armies on the Hexi and Huanqing circuits, and was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 修《儀天曆》上之，又嘗纂天文曆書為十二卷以獻，改殿中丞，賜金紫，俄權監事。

translations.literal: He revised the "Yitian Calendar" and submitted it; he also once compiled an astronomical calendar book in twelve juan and presented it; he was changed to Palace Supervisory Commissioner, granted gold and purple, and soon acted as administrator of directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the Yitian Calendar and submitted it to the throne, also compiled a twelve-juan book on astronomy and calendrics for presentation, was promoted to Palace Supervisory Commissioner, granted gold and purple insignia, and soon served as acting administrator of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 景德二年遷權知少監，大中祥符初即真。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he was promoted to acting Vice Director; at the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was promoted to acting Vice Director of the Astronomical Directorate, and at the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 序慎密勤職，在監三十年，未嘗有過，眾賴稱之。

translations.literal: Xu was careful, discreet, and diligent in office; he was at the directorate thirty years and never had a fault; the multitude relied on and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was careful, discreet, and diligent in office; he served at the directorate for thirty years without a single fault, and his colleagues relied on and praised him.

sentences.zh: 周克明字昭文。

translations.literal: Zhou Keming, styled Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Keming, styled Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖德扶，唐司農卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Defu was Tang Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Defu served as Tang Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 祖傑，開成中進士，解褐獲嘉尉，曆弘文館校書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jie was a jinshi in the Kaicheng period, began office as captain of Huojia County, and passed through collator in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jie passed the jinshi examination in the Kaicheng period, began his career as captain of Huojia County, and later served as collator in the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 中和中，僖宗在蜀，傑上書言治亂萬餘言。

translations.literal: In the Zhonghe period, when Emperor Xizong was in Shu, Jie submitted a memorial on order and disorder of more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe period, when Emperor Xizong was in Shu, Jie submitted a memorial of more than ten thousand words on the causes of order and disorder.

sentences.zh: 擢水部員外郎，三遷司農少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Water Ministry and was transferred three times to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Water Ministry and after three transfers rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 傑精於曆算，嘗以《大衍曆》數有差，因敷衍其法，著《極衍》二十四篇，以究天地之數。

translations.literal: Jie was skilled in calendar calculation; once, because the numbers of the "Dayan Calendar" had errors, he therefore elaborated its methods and wrote twenty-four chapters of "Extreme Extension" to investigate heaven-and-earth numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was skilled in calendrical calculation; finding errors in the numbers of the Dayan Calendar, he elaborated its methods and wrote twenty-four chapters of "Extreme Extension" to investigate the numbers of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 時天下方亂，傑以天文占之，惟嶺南可以避地，乃遣其弟鼎求為封州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was in disorder; Jie by astronomy prognosticated that only Lingnan could serve as a place to escape trouble, and therefore sent his younger brother Ding to seek appointment as recording officer of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was in turmoil, Jie read the heavens and concluded that only Lingnan offered refuge; he therefore sent his younger brother Ding to seek appointment as recording officer of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 傑天復中亦棄官攜家南適嶺表。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu period Jie also abandoned office, brought his family, and went south to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu period Jie also resigned his office, took his family, and moved south to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 劉隱素聞其名，每令占候天文災變。

translations.literal: Liu Yin had long heard his name and each time ordered him to prognosticate heavenly calamities and transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin had long heard of his reputation and repeatedly ordered him to prognosticate celestial calamities and portents.

sentences.zh: 傑自以年老，嘗策名中朝，恥以星曆事僭偽，乃謝病不出。

translations.literal: Jie considered himself old, had once held official name in the central court, and was ashamed to do star-and-calendar work for usurping false [regimes]; therefore he pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, considering himself old and having once held office at the central court, was ashamed to practice astronomy and calendrics for a usurping regime and therefore pleaded illness and refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 襲位，強起之，令知司天監事，因問國祚脩短。

translations.literal: Liu Chang succeeded to the throne, forcibly raised him, ordered him to administer Astronomical Directorate affairs, and thereby asked about the length and shortness of the state's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang succeeded to the throne, he forcibly summoned Jie back to service, put him in charge of Astronomical Directorate affairs, and asked how long the dynasty would endure.

sentences.zh: 傑以《周易》筮之，得《比》之《復》，曰：「卦有二土，土數生五，成於十，二五相比，以歲言之，當五百五十。」

translations.literal: Jie by the "Book of Changes" divined and obtained Bi changing to Fu; he said: "The hexagram has two earth [lines]; earth's number generates five and completes at ten; two and five compare with each other—speaking in years, it should be five hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Jie divined with the Book of Changes and obtained Bi changing to Fu; he said, "The hexagram contains two earth lines; the number of earth generates five and completes at ten; two and five stand in mutual relation—counted in years, the span should be five hundred fifty.

sentences.zh: 大喜，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Liu Chang greatly rejoiced and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang was greatly pleased and rewarded him very generously.

sentences.zh: 以梁貞明三年僭號，至開寶四年國滅，止五十五年。

translations.literal: Liu Chang from the third year of Liang Zhenming usurped the title; reaching the fourth year of Kaibao the state was destroyed—only fifty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang's regime had usurped imperial title in the third year of Liang Zhenming; by the fourth year of Kaibao the state was destroyed—only fifty-five years in all.

sentences.zh: 蓋傑舉成數以避害爾。

translations.literal: Probably Jie cited a round number to avoid harm, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had simply chosen a flattering round number to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 大有中，遷太常少卿，卒，年九十餘。

translations.literal: In the Dayou period he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he died at age ninety-plus.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dayou period he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 傑生茂元，亦世其學，事至司天少監，歸宋授監丞而卒，即克明之父也。

translations.literal: Jie had Maoyuan, who also inherited the learning generation after generation, served Liu Chang reaching Astronomical Vice Director, submitted to Song and was appointed supervising commissioner then died—he was Keming's father.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's son Maoyuan also inherited the family art, served Liu Chang until he reached the post of Vice Director of the Astronomical Directorate, submitted to the Song and was appointed supervising commissioner before his death—he was Keming's father.

sentences.zh: 克明精於數術，凡律曆、天官、五行、讖緯及三式、風雲、龜筮之書，靡不究其指要。

translations.literal: Keming was skilled in number arts; every book on pitch pipes and calendars, celestial bureaucracy, five phases, prophecies and weft texts, Three Styles, wind and cloud, and tortoise and milfoil—none he did not investigate to their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was skilled in the numerical arts and mastered the essentials of every branch of learning—from pitch pipes and calendars, celestial offices, and the five phases to prophecy texts, the Three Styles, wind and cloud divination, and tortoise and milfoil oracle books.

sentences.zh: 開寶中授司天六壬，改台主簿，轉監丞，五遷春官正。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he was appointed Six Ren officer of the Astronomical Directorate, changed to Spirit Platform chief clerk, transferred to supervising commissioner, and was promoted five times to Spring Office Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao he was appointed Six Ren officer of the Astronomical Directorate, then served as Spirit Platform chief clerk, supervising commissioner, and after five promotions became Spring Office Director.

sentences.zh: 克明頗修詞藻，喜藏書。

translations.literal: Keming quite cultivated literary elegance and delighted in collecting books.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was also accomplished in literary composition and delighted in collecting books.

sentences.zh: 景德初，嘗獻所著文十編，召試中書，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he once presented his own writings in ten compilations, was summoned to examination at the Secretariat, and was granted jinshi status by special decree.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde era he presented ten compilations of his own writings, was summoned to examination at the Secretariat, and was granted jinshi status by special decree.

sentences.zh: 三年，有大星出氐西，眾莫能辨；

translations.literal: In the third year a great star appeared west of Di, and the crowd none could identify it;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a great star appeared west of the Di asterism, and no one could identify it;

sentences.zh: 或言國皇妖星，為兵凶之兆。

translations.literal: Some said it was the demon star Guohuang, an omen of military disaster.
translations.idiomatic: some said it was the demon star Guohuang, a portent of war and disaster.

sentences.zh: 克明時使嶺表，及還，亟請對，言：「臣按《天文錄》、《荊州占》，其星名曰周伯，其色黃，其光煌煌然，所見之國大昌，是德星也。

translations.literal: Keming was then on mission to Lingnan; when he returned he urgently requested audience and said: "Your subject, examining the "Astronomical Records" and "Jingzhou Prognostications," finds its star name is Zhou Bo; its color is yellow, its light brilliant; the country that sees it greatly prospers—it is a virtue star.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was then on mission to Lingnan; when he returned he urgently requested an audience and said, "Your subject has consulted the Astronomical Records and Jingzhou Prognostications: the star is called Zhou Bo, its color is yellow, and its light is brilliant; the country that sees it will greatly prosper—it is a virtue star.

sentences.zh: 臣在塗聞中外之人頗惑其事，願許文武稱慶，以安天下心。」

translations.literal: Your subject on the road heard that people inside and outside were quite confused by the matter; I wish permission for civil and military officials to proclaim celebration, to settle the hearts of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the road I heard that people throughout the realm were troubled by the matter; I ask that civil and military officials be permitted to proclaim celebration and thereby reassure the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，即從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and immediately followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and immediately granted his request.

sentences.zh: 拜太子洗馬、殿中丞，皆兼翰林天文，又權判監事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Supervisory Commissioner, all concurrently Hanlin Astronomer, and also acting concurrent administrator of directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Supervisory Commissioner, both with concurrent appointment as Hanlin Astronomer, and also served as acting administrator of directorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 屬修兩朝國史，其天文律曆事，命克明參之。

translations.literal: When the Two Dynasties National History was being revised, its astronomical and calendrical matters were ordered to have Keming participate.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was compiling the national history of the two dynasties, Keming was ordered to assist with its sections on astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，坐本監擇日差互，例降為洗馬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, because of this directorate's date-selection discrepancy, by precedent he was demoted to Groom.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was demoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent under precedent for a date-selection error by the directorate.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年夏，火犯靈台，克明語所親曰：「去歲太白犯靈台，掌曆者悉被降譴，上天垂象，深可畏也。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Tianxi, Fire violated Spirit Platform; Keming told those close to him: "Last year White Metal violated Spirit Platform, and calendar keepers were all demoted and censured; Heaven displays signs—deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Tianxi, Mars entered the Spirit Platform asterism; Keming told those close to him, "Last year Venus entered the Spirit Platform, and the calendar keepers were all demoted and punished; when Heaven displays such signs, they are deeply to be feared.

sentences.zh: 今熒惑又犯之，吾其不起乎！」

translations.literal: Now Mars again violates it—probably I shall not rise!
translations.idiomatic: Now Mars has violated it again—I fear I shall not recover!

sentences.zh: 八月，疽發背，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth month a carbuncle erupted on his back; he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a carbuncle erupted on his back, and he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 克明久居司天之職，頗勤慎，凡奏對必據經盡言。

translations.literal: Keming long held the Astronomical post, was quite diligent and careful, and whenever memorializing or answering always based himself on the classics and spoke fully.
translations.idiomatic: Keming long held office in the Astronomical Directorate, was diligent and careful, and whenever he addressed the throne he spoke fully and always grounded his words in the classics.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上頗悼惜，遣內侍諭其婿直龍圖閣馮元，令主喪事，賜賻甚厚。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor was quite mournful and regretful, sent a palace attendant to instruct his son-in-law Direct Longtu Pavilion Feng Yuan to manage the funeral, and granted burial gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor was deeply grieved, sent a palace attendant to instruct his son-in-law Feng Yuan, Director of the Longtu Pavilion, to manage the funeral, and granted a very generous burial gift.

sentences.zh: 初，諸僭國皆有纂錄，獨嶺南闕焉。

translations.literal: Initially, all usurping states had compiled records; only Lingnan lacked them.
translations.idiomatic: At first every separatist regime had its history compiled, but Lingnan alone had none.

sentences.zh: 惟胡賓王、胡元興二家纂述，皆不之備。

translations.literal: Only the two families of Hu Binwang and Hu Yuanxing compiled narratives, and all were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Only the works compiled by Hu Binwang and Hu Yuanxing existed, and neither was complete.

sentences.zh: 克明訪耆舊，采碑誌，孳孳著撰，裁十數卷，書未成而卒。

translations.literal: Keming visited elders, gathered stele inscriptions, diligently wrote and compiled, cut to ten-plus juan, and the book was not finished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Keming interviewed elders, collected stele inscriptions, and worked diligently at writing, producing more than ten juan before he died with the book still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 劉翰，滄州臨津人。

translations.literal: Liu Han was a native of Linjin in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Han was a native of Linjin in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世習醫業，初攝護國軍節度巡官。

translations.literal: His family practiced medicine for generations; he initially served as adjutant patrol officer of the Huguo Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His family had practiced medicine for generations; he first served as adjutant patrol officer under the Huguo Army military commission.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，詣闕獻《經用方書》三十卷、《論候》十卷、《今體治世集》二十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Xiande, he went to the court and presented thirty juan of Essential Prescriptions for Regular Use, ten juan of Treatises on Diagnosis, and twenty juan of A Collection on Contemporary Forms of Governing the Age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande reign of Later Zhou, he went to court and presented thirty juan of Essential Prescriptions for Regular Use, ten juan of Treatises on Diagnosis, and twenty juan of A Collection on Contemporary Forms of Governing the Age.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉之，命為翰林醫官，其書付史館，再加衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong praised this, ordered him appointed Hanlin medical officer, his books delivered to the Historiography Institute, and further added Court of Imperial Regalia registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong commended him, appointed him a Hanlin medical officer, had his books deposited in the Historiography Institute, and further promoted him to registrar of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 太祖北征，命翰從行。

translations.literal: When Taizu marched north on campaign, he ordered Han to accompany the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu marched north on campaign, he ordered Han to accompany the army.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，加朝散大夫、鴻臚寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, he was further given Grand Master of Dispersed Leisure and vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianlong reign, he was further promoted to Grand Master of Dispersed Leisure and vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 時太祖求治，事皆核實，故方技之士必精練。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu sought good governance, and affairs were all verified for substance, so practitioners of technical arts had to be thoroughly skilled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taizu sought to govern well and insisted that every matter be verified in substance, so specialists in medicine and divination had to be thoroughly accomplished.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，令太常寺考較翰林醫官藝術，以翰為優，絀其業不精者二十六人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine and compare the medical skills of Hanlin medical officers; Han was judged superior, and twenty-six whose craft was not refined were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qiande reign, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to examine and rank the skills of Hanlin medical officers; Han was judged the best, and twenty-six whose skills were found deficient were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 自後，又詔諸州訪醫術優長者籍其名，仍量賜裝錢，所在廚傳給食，遣詣闕。

translations.literal: Afterward, an edict again ordered the prefectures to seek out those outstanding in medical skill, register their names, also grant traveling funds in due measure, supply food at relay stations along the way, and send them to court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter an edict ordered every prefecture to seek out physicians of outstanding skill, register their names, grant them traveling expenses as appropriate, provide meals at relay stations along the route, and send them to court.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，太宗在藩邸有疾，命翰與馬誌視之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, the Prince of Jin fell ill at his princely residence, and Han and Ma Zhi were ordered to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao, the future Emperor Taizong fell ill at his princely residence, and Han and Ma Zhi were ordered to treat him.

sentences.zh: 及愈，轉尚藥奉御，賜銀器、緡錢、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: When he recovered, Han was transferred to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy, and was granted silver vessels, cash, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince recovered, Han was promoted to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy and was granted silver vessels, cash, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 嘗被詔詳定《唐本草》，翰與道士馬誌、醫官翟煦、張素、吳復珪圭、王光祐、陳昭遇同議，凡《神農本經》三百六十種，《名醫錄》一百八十二種，唐本先附一百一十四種，有名無用一百九十四種，翰等又參定新附一百三十三種。

translations.literal: He was once ordered by edict to collate and fix the Tang Materia Medica; Han together with the Daoist Ma Zhi and the medical officers Zhai Xu, Zhang Su, Wu Fugui, Wang Guangyou, and Chen Zhaoyu jointly deliberated. In all there were three hundred sixty kinds from Shennong's Root Classic, one hundred eighty-two kinds from Records of Famous Physicians, one hundred fourteen kinds in the Tang edition's first appendix, one hundred ninety-four kinds listed by name but useless, and Han and the others further collated one hundred thirty-three newly appended kinds.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to collate the Tang Materia Medica. Han joined the Daoist Ma Zhi and the medical officers Zhai Xu, Zhang Su, Wu Fugui, Wang Guangyou, and Chen Zhaoyu in the work. The text included three hundred sixty entries from Shennong's Root Classic, one hundred eighty-two from Records of Famous Physicians, one hundred fourteen in the Tang edition's first appendix, and one hundred ninety-four listed by name but deemed useless; Han and his colleagues further collated one hundred thirty-three newly appended entries.

sentences.zh: 既成，詔翰林學士中書舍人李昉、戶部員外郎知制誥王祐、左司員外郎知制誥扈蒙詳覆畢上之。

translations.literal: When it was finished, Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter Li Fang, vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts Wang You, and vice director of the Left Department and drafter of edicts Hu Meng were ordered to review it in detail and submit it when complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, Li Fang, Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter; Wang You, vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts; and Hu Meng, vice director of the Left Department and drafter of edicts, were ordered to review it thoroughly and submit the final version.

sentences.zh: 昉等序之曰：

translations.literal: Li Fang and the others prefaced it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang and his colleagues wrote a preface, saying:

sentences.zh: 《三墳》之書，神農預其一。

translations.literal: Among the books of the Three Sovereigns' tombs, Shennong was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the books ascribed to the Three Sovereigns, Shennong's work was one.

sentences.zh: 百藥即辨，《本草》序其錄。

translations.literal: The hundred drugs were then distinguished, and the Materia Medica ordered their entries.
translations.idiomatic: When the myriad drugs had been distinguished, the Materia Medica arranged them in ordered entries.

sentences.zh: 舊經三卷，世所流傳。

translations.literal: The old classic was three juan, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The original classic, in three juan, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 《名醫別錄》，互為編纂。

translations.literal: Separate Records of Famous Physicians was mutually compiled with it.
translations.idiomatic: Separate Records of Famous Physicians was compiled alongside it.

sentences.zh: 至梁陶弘景乃以《別錄》參其《本經》，朱墨雜書，時謂明白。

translations.literal: When it came to Liang, Tao Hongjing then used the Separate Records to compare with the Root Classic, writing in red and black mixed, and contemporaries called it clear.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang times Tao Hongjing collated the Separate Records with the Root Classic, marking the texts in red and black, and contemporaries praised the result as lucid.

sentences.zh: 而又考彼功用，為之注釋，列為七卷，南國行焉。

translations.literal: He also examined their functions, made annotations for them, arranged them in seven juan, and they circulated in the southern states.
translations.idiomatic: He further examined their medicinal properties, supplied annotations, arranged the work in seven juan, and it circulated throughout the southern states.

sentences.zh: 逮乎有唐，別加參校，增藥餘八百味，添注為二十卷。

translations.literal: When there came Tang, they separately added collation, adding more than eight hundred drugs in annotations to twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times the text was again collated, more than eight hundred drugs were added, and the annotated edition was expanded to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 《本經》漏缺則補之，陶氏誤說則證之。

translations.literal: Where the Root Classic had omissions and gaps they supplemented them; where Master Tao's mistaken statements were, they verified them.
translations.idiomatic: Omissions and gaps in the Root Classic were filled in, and erroneous statements by Master Tao were corrected by verification.

sentences.zh: 然而載曆年祀，又逾四百，朱字墨字，無本得同；

translations.literal: Yet carrying on through years and ages, again exceeding four hundred years, red characters and black characters—no edition could match;
translations.idiomatic: Yet more than four hundred years had passed, and with red text and black text alike, no two copies agreed;

sentences.zh: 舊注新注，其文互闕。

translations.literal: Old annotations and new annotations, their text mutually lacked parts.
translations.idiomatic: Old annotations and new annotations were incomplete and inconsistent with one another.

sentences.zh: 非聖主撫大同之運，永無疆之休，其何以改而正之哉！

translations.literal: Were it not for a sage lord embracing the fortune of great unity and everlasting boundless felicity, how could one reform and correct them!
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for a sage ruler who embraced the fortune of universal harmony and everlasting peace, how could the text have been reformed and set right!

sentences.zh: 乃命盡考傳誤，刊為定本。

translations.literal: He then ordered a thorough examination of transmitted errors and publication of a fixed edition.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore ordered a full examination of transmitted errors and the publication of an authoritative edition.

sentences.zh: 類例非允，從而革焉。

translations.literal: Categories and examples that were not acceptable were thereupon reformed.
