translations.idiomatic: Where the categories and classifications were unsatisfactory, they were revised accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至如筆頭灰，兔毫也，而在草部，今移附兔頭骨之下；

translations.literal: As for brush-tip ash, it is rabbit hair, yet it was in the herbs section; now it is moved and appended below rabbit skull;
translations.idiomatic: Brush-tip ash, for example, is rabbit hair, yet it had been placed in the herbs section; it is now moved and placed under rabbit skull;

sentences.zh: 半天河、地漿，皆水也，亦在草部，今移附土石類之間；

translations.literal: Celestial river water and earth broth are both water, yet were also in the herbs section; now they are moved and appended among earth and stone categories;
translations.idiomatic: Celestial river water and earth broth are both forms of water, yet they too had been listed among herbs; they are now moved among the earth and stone entries;

sentences.zh: 敗鼓皮，移附於獸名；

translations.literal: Decayed drum hide is moved and appended under beast names;
translations.idiomatic: Decayed drum hide is now placed under animal products;

sentences.zh: 胡桐淚，改從於木類；

translations.literal: Poplar resin is changed to follow the wood category;
translations.idiomatic: Poplar resin is reclassified under woods;

sentences.zh: 紫礦，亦木也，自玉石品而改焉；

translations.literal: Purple ore is also a wood; it is changed from the jade and stone category;
translations.idiomatic: Purple lac, which is also a tree product, is moved out of the jades and stones;

sentences.zh: 伏翼，實禽也，由蟲魚部而移焉；

translations.literal: Hidden wings are in fact birds; they are moved from the insects and fish section;
translations.idiomatic: The bat, which is in fact a bird, is moved out of the insects and fish section;

sentences.zh: 橘柚，附於果實；

translations.literal: Oranges and pomelos are appended to fruits;
translations.idiomatic: Oranges and pomelos are grouped with fruits;

sentences.zh: 食鹽，附於光鹽；

translations.literal: Edible salt is appended to light salt;
translations.idiomatic: Table salt is grouped with light salt;

sentences.zh: 生薑、乾薑，同歸一類；

translations.literal: Fresh ginger and dried ginger are together returned to one category;
translations.idiomatic: Fresh ginger and dried ginger are placed in a single category;

sentences.zh: 至於雞腸、蘩蔞，陸英、蒴藋，以類相似，從而附之。

translations.literal: As for chicken intestine, chickweed, boneset, and teasel, because their categories were similar, they were accordingly appended together.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken intestine, chickweed, boneset, and teasel, being of similar kind, were likewise grouped together.

sentences.zh: 仍采陳藏器《拾遺》、李含光《音義》，或窮源於別本，或傳效於醫家，參而較之，辨其臧否。

translations.literal: They still drew on Chen Cangqi's Supplementary Records and Li Hanguang's Phonetic and Semantic Notes, sometimes tracing sources in separate editions, sometimes transmitting efficacy from medical families, comparing them together and distinguishing what was good and what was not.
translations.idiomatic: They also drew on Chen Cangqi's Supplementary Records and Li Hanguang's Phonetic and Semantic Notes, tracing some entries to alternate editions and others to medical practitioners' experience, then compared the evidence and judged what was valid and what was not.

sentences.zh: 至如突屈白，舊說灰類，今是木根；

translations.literal: As for tuju bai, the old account said it was an ash category; now it is a tree root;
translations.idiomatic: Tuju bai, for example, had formerly been described as an ash product but is now identified as a tree root;

sentences.zh: 天麻根，解似赤箭，今又全異。

translations.literal: Gastrodia root was explained as resembling red arrow, yet now it is wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Gastrodia root had been explained as identical with red arrow, but is now shown to be entirely distinct.

sentences.zh: 去非取是，特立新條。

translations.literal: Removing what was wrong and taking what was right, they specially established new entries.
translations.idiomatic: Rejecting error and affirming truth, they established new entries of their own.

sentences.zh: 自餘刊正，不可悉數。

translations.literal: As for the remaining corrections and revisions, they cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining corrections are too numerous to list in full.

sentences.zh: 下采眾議，定為印板。

translations.literal: Below they gathered public deliberation and fixed it as a printed edition.
translations.idiomatic: After consulting widely, they fixed the text for printing.

sentences.zh: 乃以白字為神農所說，墨字為名醫所傳，唐附今附，各加顯注，詳其解釋，審其形性。

translations.literal: They then used white characters for what Shennong spoke, black characters for what famous physicians transmitted, Tang appendices and present appendices each with added explicit notes, detailing their explanations and examining their form and nature.
translations.idiomatic: White characters mark what Shennong is said to have stated, black characters what famous physicians transmitted; Tang and present appendices each receive explicit notes, with full explanations and careful identification of form and properties.

sentences.zh: 證謬誤而辨之者，署為今注；

translations.literal: Those that verified errors and distinguished them are signed as present notes;
translations.idiomatic: Notes that verify and correct errors are marked as present annotations;

sentences.zh: 考文意而述之者，又為今按。

translations.literal: Those that examined textual meaning and set it forth are further made present commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Commentaries that examine textual meaning and explain it are marked as present commentaries.

sentences.zh: 義既判定，理亦詳明。

translations.literal: The meaning having been decided, the principle is also detailed and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning has been settled and principle set forth in full clarity.

sentences.zh: 今以新舊藥合九百八十三種，並目錄二十一卷，廣頒天下，傳而行焉。

translations.literal: Now old and new drugs together total nine hundred eighty-three kinds, with table of contents in twenty-one juan, broadly distributed throughout the realm, transmitted and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The edition now comprises nine hundred eighty-three old and new drugs in twenty-one juan including the table of contents, to be distributed throughout the realm and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 翰後加檢校工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Han was afterward further given acting vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Han was later given the additional title of acting vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，命為翰林醫官使，再加檢校戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, he was ordered appointed Hanlin medical commissioner, and further given acting director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was appointed Hanlin medical commissioner and further given the additional title of acting director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，滑州劉遇疾，詔翰馳往視之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Liu Yu of Huazhou fell ill, and Han was ordered to hurry there to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Liu Yu of Huazhou fell ill, and Han was ordered to go at once to treat him.

sentences.zh: 翰還，言遇必瘳，既而即死，坐責授和州團練副使。

translations.literal: Han returned and said Yu would certainly recover; soon afterward he immediately died. For this he was punished and appointed deputy military commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han returned and reported that Liu Yu would certainly recover, but Liu Yu died shortly afterward; for this Han was punished and demoted to deputy military commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，起為尚藥奉御。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was raised to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong reign he was restored to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，復為醫官使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, he again became medical commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua he was again appointed medical commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 王懷隱，宋州睢陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Huaiyin was a native of Suiyang in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaiyin was a native of Suiyang in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為道士，住京城建隆觀，善醫診。

translations.literal: He was initially a Daoist priest, residing at the Jianlong Abbey in the capital, skilled in medical diagnosis.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally a Daoist priest at the Jianlong Abbey in the capital and was skilled in diagnosis.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，懷隱以湯劑祗事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin governed the capital, Huaiyin respectfully served him with decoctions.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Taizong governed the capital, Huaiyin attended him with medicinal decoctions.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，詔歸俗，命為尚藥奉御，三遷至翰林醫官使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was ordered to return to secular life, appointed chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy, and promoted three times to Hanlin medical commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was ordered to leave the priesthood, appointed chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy, and promoted three times until he reached the post of Hanlin medical commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年。

translations.literal: The third year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of that reign,

sentences.zh: 吳越遣子惟濬入朝，惟濬被疾，詔懷隱視之。

translations.literal: Wuyue sent the prince Weijun to court; Weijun fell ill, and Huaiyin was ordered to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue sent Prince Weijun to court; when Weijun fell ill, Huaiyin was ordered to treat him.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗在藩邸，暇日多留意醫術，藏名方千餘首，皆嘗有驗者。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Prince of Jin was at his princely residence, in leisure days he often paid attention to medical arts, storing more than a thousand famous formulas, all of which had once been effective.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still at his princely residence, the future Emperor Taizong had often devoted his leisure to medicine and collected more than a thousand proven prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔翰林醫官院各具家傳經驗方以獻，又萬餘首，命懷隱與副使王祐、鄭奇、醫官陳昭遇參對編類。

translations.literal: At this time, the Hanlin Medical Institute was ordered each to submit family-transmitted experiential formulas, again more than ten thousand formulas; Huaiyin together with deputy commissioner Wang You, Zheng Qi, and medical officer Chen Zhaoyu were ordered to collate and classify them by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Hanlin Medical Institute was ordered to submit its physicians' family prescriptions and experiential formulas, yielding more than ten thousand additional entries; Huaiyin, together with deputy commissioner Wang You, Zheng Qi, and medical officer Chen Zhaoyu, was ordered to collate and classify them.

sentences.zh: 每部以隋太醫令巢元方《病源候論》冠其首，而方藥次之，成一百卷。

translations.literal: Each section took Sui grand medical director Chao Yuanfang's Treatise on the Origins and Manifestations of Diseases as its head, with formulas and drugs following after, forming one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: Each section opened with the Sui grand medical director Chao Yuanfang's Treatise on the Origins and Manifestations of Diseases, followed by prescriptions and drugs, producing a work of one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 太宗御製序，賜名曰《太平聖惠方》，仍令鏤板頒行天下，諸州各置醫博士掌之。

translations.literal: Taizong personally composed the preface, bestowed the name Imperial Formulas of the Taiping Sacred Beneficence, and further ordered it carved on blocks and distributed throughout the realm; each prefecture was to establish a medical director to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wrote the preface himself, named the work Imperial Formulas of the Taiping Sacred Beneficence, ordered it carved and printed for distribution throughout the realm, and directed each prefecture to appoint a medical director to oversee its use.

sentences.zh: 懷隱後數年卒。

translations.literal: Huaiyin died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin died several years later.

sentences.zh: 昭遇本嶺南人，醫術尤精驗，初為醫官，領溫水主簿，後加光錄寺丞，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Zhaoyu was originally a man of Lingnan, his medical art especially refined and proven; he was initially a medical officer, concurrently serving as registrar of Wenshui, later added director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyu was a native of Lingnan and was especially accomplished in medicine. He first served as a medical officer while also holding the post of registrar of Wenshui, was later promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 趙自化，本德州平原人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zihua was originally a man of Pingyuan in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zihua was originally from Pingyuan in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖常，為景州刺史，後舉家陷契丹。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang served as prefect of Jingzhou; afterward the whole family fell into the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had served as prefect of Jingzhou, but later the entire family fell into Khitan hands.

sentences.zh: 父知嵓脫身南歸，寓居洛陽，習經方名藥之術，又以授二子自正、自化。

translations.literal: His father Zhuyan escaped south and returned, sojourned in Luoyang, studied the arts of classical formulas and famous drugs, and also taught his two sons Zizheng and Zihua.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuyan escaped and returned south, settled in Luoyang, mastered classical prescriptions and celebrated drugs, and passed the art on to his two sons Zizheng and Zihua.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，偕來京師，悉以醫術稱。

translations.literal: In Zhou Xiande, they together came to the capital, and all were famed for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign of Later Zhou they came together to the capital, and both were celebrated for their medical skill.

sentences.zh: 知嵓卒，自正試方技，補翰林醫學。

translations.literal: When Zhuyan died, Zizheng was tested in technical arts and appointed Hanlin medical student.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuyan died, Zizheng passed the examination in medicine and divination and was appointed a Hanlin medical student.

sentences.zh: 會秦國長公主疾，有薦自化診候者，疾愈，表為醫學，再加尚藥奉御。

translations.literal: When the Princess of Qin fell ill, someone recommended Zihua to diagnose and observe her; when the illness recovered, he was memorialized as medical student and further made chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Qin fell ill, someone recommended Zihua to examine her; after she recovered he was appointed a medical student and later promoted to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，授醫官副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, he was appointed deputy medical commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was appointed deputy medical commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時召陳州隱士萬適至，館於自化家。

translations.literal: At that time the reclusive scholar Wan Shi of Chenzhou was summoned and lodged at Zihua's home.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Chenzhou recluse Wan Shi was summoned to court and lodged in Zihua's household.

sentences.zh: 會以適補慎縣主簿，適素強力無疾，詔下日，自化怪其色變，為切脈曰：「君將死矣。」

translations.literal: It happened that Shi was appointed registrar of Shen County; Shi had always been strong and without illness, but on the day the edict was issued, Zihua wondered at his changed complexion, took his pulse, and said: "You are about to die."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was appointed registrar of Shen County, he had always been robust and free of illness; yet on the day the edict arrived Zihua was struck by the change in his complexion, felt his pulse, and said, "You are going to die."

sentences.zh: 不數日，適果卒。

translations.literal: Within a few days, Shi indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Shi did indeed die.

sentences.zh: 至道中，有布衣鄭元輔者，嘗依自化之姻吏部令史張崇敏家。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao reign, there was a commoner named Zheng Yuanfu who had once relied on Zihua's affinal relation, Ministry of Personnel clerk Zhang Chongmin, for lodging.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao reign a commoner named Zheng Yuanfu had once lived as a dependent in the household of Zhang Chongmin, a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and a relative by marriage of Zihua.

sentences.zh: 元輔時從自化丐索，無所得，心銜之。

translations.literal: Yuanfu often begged and sought things from Zihua but obtained nothing, and harbored resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu had often begged favors from Zihua without success and nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 乃詣檢上書，告自化漏泄禁中語及指斥、非所宜言等事。

translations.literal: He then went to the censorate and submitted a memorial, accusing Zihua of leaking palace speech and of pointing out and saying what was not fitting to say, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the censorate and submitted a memorial accusing Zihua of leaking palace secrets and of making improper and slanderous remarks.

sentences.zh: 太宗初甚駭，命王繼恩就御史府鞫之，皆無狀，斬元輔於都市。

translations.literal: Taizong at first was greatly alarmed and ordered Wang Jien to go to the censorate to interrogate the case; all was without substance, and Yuanfu was executed in the market of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was at first greatly alarmed and ordered Wang Jien to investigate the case at the censorate; the charges proved entirely false, and Yuanfu was executed in the capital marketplace.

sentences.zh: 自化坐交遊非類，黜為郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: Zihua, convicted of associating with improper persons, was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua was punished for keeping improper company and was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復舊職。

translations.literal: Before long, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，加正使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, he was further made chief commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was promoted to chief medical commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自化頗喜為篇什，其貶郢州也，有《漢沔詩集》五卷，宋白、李若拙為之序。

translations.literal: Zihua quite liked composing verse; when he was demoted to Yingzhou, he had five juan of Han and Mian Poetry Collection, for which Song Bai and Li Ruozhuo wrote prefaces.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua was fond of writing poetry; during his demotion to Yingzhou he compiled five juan of Han and Mian Poetry Collection, for which Song Bai and Li Ruozhuo wrote prefaces.

sentences.zh: 又嘗纘自古以方技至貴仕者，為《名醫顯秩傳》三卷。

translations.literal: He also once compiled those from antiquity who through technical arts reached honored office, making three juan of Biographies of Famous Physicians in Distinguished Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a three-juan Biographies of Famous Physicians in Distinguished Rank, recording physicians from antiquity onward who had risen through medicine and divination to high office.

sentences.zh: 馮文智，并州人。

translations.literal: Feng Wenzhi was a man of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Wenzhi was a native of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世以方技為業。

translations.literal: His family took technical arts as their profession.
translations.idiomatic: His family had practiced medicine and divination for generations.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中詣都自陳，召試補醫學，加樂源縣主簿。

translations.literal: In Taiping Xingguo he went to the capital and presented himself, was summoned for examination and appointed medical student, and further given registrar of Leyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he went to the capital to offer his services, passed the examination, was appointed a medical student, and was also given the post of registrar of Leyuan County.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，授少府監主簿，逾年轉醫官，加少府監丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was appointed registrar of the Directorate of Palace Manufactories; after a year he was transferred to medical officer and further given vice director of the Directorate of Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed registrar of the Directorate of Palace Manufactories; a year later he was transferred to medical officer and promoted to vice director of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘗隸並代部署。

translations.literal: He once served under the Bingdai headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He once served on the staff of the Bingdai headquarters.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，府州折禦卿疾，文智診療獲愈，禦卿表薦之，賜緋，加光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Zhe Yuqing of Fuzhou fell ill; Wenzhi diagnosed and treated him and he recovered. Yuqing memorialized recommending him, and he was granted crimson robe and made director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Zhe Yuqing of Fuzhou fell ill; Wenzhi treated him successfully. Yuqing submitted a recommendation, and Wenzhi was granted a crimson robe and promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，明德太后不豫，文智侍醫，既愈，加尚藥奉御，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, Empress Dowager Mingde was unwell; Wenzhi attended as physician, and when she recovered he was further made chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping, Empress Dowager Mingde fell ill; Wenzhi served as her attending physician, and after she recovered he was promoted to chief attendant of the Imperial Pharmacy and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 六年，直翰林醫官院。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he served directly in the Hanlin Medical Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was assigned directly to the Hanlin Medical Institute.

sentences.zh: 東封，轉醫官副使。

translations.literal: On the eastern feng, he was transferred to deputy medical commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern tour of Mount Tai he was promoted to deputy medical commissioner.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，又加檢校主客員外郎。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was further given acting vice director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice at Fenyin he was further given the additional title of acting vice director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 自建隆以來，近臣皇親、諸大校有疾，必遣內侍挾醫療視，群臣中有特被眷遇者亦如之。

translations.literal: From Jianlong onward, when close ministers, imperial kin, and major commanders fell ill, inner attendants were always sent carrying physicians to treat and examine them; among the ministers, those especially favored were likewise treated.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianlong onward, whenever close ministers, imperial relatives, or senior commanders fell ill, palace attendants were dispatched with physicians to treat them; favored ministers received the same care.

sentences.zh: 其有效者，或遷秩、賜服色。

translations.literal: Those who were effective might be transferred in rank or granted robe colors.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians who succeeded might be promoted or granted honorary robe colors.

sentences.zh: 邊郡屯帥多遣醫官、醫學隨行，三年一代。

translations.literal: Border prefecture garrison commanders mostly sent medical officers and medical students to accompany them, replaced every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of border garrisons generally had medical officers and medical students attached to their staffs, rotated every three years.

sentences.zh: 出師及使境外、貢院鎖宿，皆令醫官隨之。

translations.literal: On military expeditions and missions beyond the borders, and during locked lodging in examination halls, medical officers were all ordered to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: Medical officers accompanied troops on campaign, envoys abroad, and candidates during the locked seclusion of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 京城四面，分遣翰林祗候療視將士。

translations.literal: On the four sides of the capital, Hanlin attendants were separately dispatched to treat and examine soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On all four sides of the capital, Hanlin attendants were dispatched to treat the troops.

sentences.zh: 暑月，即令醫官合藥，與內侍分詣城門寺院散給軍民。

translations.literal: In summer months, medical officers were immediately ordered to compound medicines, and together with inner attendants separately went to city gates and temples to distribute them to soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: During the hot summer months, medical officers were ordered to prepare medicines and, together with palace attendants, sent to city gates and temples throughout the capital to distribute them to soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 上每便坐閱兵，有被金瘡者，即令醫官處療。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor reviewed troops at informal sessions, if anyone had metal wounds, he immediately ordered medical officers to treat them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor reviewed the troops in informal session, anyone with a wound from blade or arrow was immediately sent to a medical officer for treatment.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，有軍士嘗中流矢，自頰貫耳，眾醫不能取，醫官閻文顯以藥傅之，信宿而鏃出。

translations.literal: During Xianping, a soldier was once struck by a crossbow bolt that passed through his cheek and pierced his ear; many physicians could not remove it; medical officer Yan Wenxian applied medicine to it, and within two nights the arrowhead came out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, a soldier was hit by a crossbow bolt that passed through his cheek and pierced his ear. No physician could extract it, but medical officer Yan Wenxian applied a poultice, and within two days the arrowhead worked free.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其能，命賜緋。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his ability and ordered crimson robes granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his skill and ordered that he be granted the crimson robe.

sentences.zh: 又有醫學劉贇亦善此術。

translations.literal: Also medical student Liu Yun was skilled in this technique.
translations.idiomatic: Medical student Liu Yun was also adept at this art.

sentences.zh: 天武右廂都指揮使韓晸從太祖征晉陽，弩矢貫左髀，鏃不出幾三十年。

translations.literal: Han Jiao, commander-in-chief of the Right Wing of the Celestial Martial Guard, accompanied Taizu on the campaign against Jinyang; a crossbow bolt pierced his left thigh, and the arrowhead did not come out for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiao, commander-in-chief of the Right Wing of the Celestial Martial Guard, had accompanied Taizu on the campaign against Jinyang when a crossbow bolt pierced his left thigh. The arrowhead remained embedded for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 景德初，上遣贇視晸，贇傅以藥出之，步履如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, the emperor sent Yun to examine Jiao; Yun applied medicine and extracted it, and his gait was as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde era, the emperor sent Yun to treat Jiao. Yun applied a medicinal poultice and removed the arrowhead, and Jiao walked as he had before.

sentences.zh: 晸請見，自陳感激，願得死所，又極稱贇之妙。

translations.literal: Jiao requested an audience, expressed gratitude himself, said he wished to die in service, and also lavishly praised Yun's skill.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao requested an audience, poured out his gratitude, declared that he wished to die in the emperor's service, and spoke at length of Yun's extraordinary skill.

sentences.zh: 特賜贇白金，遷醫官。

translations.literal: Yun was specially granted white gold and transferred to medical officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was specially rewarded with white gold and promoted to medical officer.

sentences.zh: 沙門洪蘊，本姓藍，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: The Buddhist monk Hongyun, original surname Lan, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist monk Hongyun, whose original surname was Lan, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 母翁，初以無子，專誦佛經，既而有娠，生洪蘊。

translations.literal: His mother Weng, initially because she had no son, devoted herself to reciting Buddhist sutras; afterward she became pregnant and bore Hongyun.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Weng had long been childless and devoted herself to reciting Buddhist sutras. She then conceived and gave birth to Hongyun.

sentences.zh: 年十三，詣郡之開福寺沙門智巴，求出家，習方技之書，後遊京師，以醫術知名。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he went to the Buddhist monk Zhiba at Kaifu Temple in the prefecture to seek ordination, studied books on medicine and divination, later traveled to the capital, and became renowned for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he went to the Buddhist monk Zhiba at Kaifu Temple in the prefecture to take ordination, studied works on medicine and divination, and later traveled to the capital, where he became famous for his medical art.

sentences.zh: 太祖召見，賜紫方袍，號廣利大師。

translations.literal: Taizu summoned him for audience, granted a purple square robe, and gave him the title Great Master Guangli.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu summoned him to court, granted him a purple square robe, and invested him with the title Great Master Guangli.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，詔購醫方，洪蘊錄古方數十以獻。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, an edict sought medical prescriptions; Hongyun recorded several tens of ancient prescriptions and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo the court issued an edict soliciting medical prescriptions, and Hongyun copied out several dozen ancient formulas and presented them.

sentences.zh: 真宗在蜀邸，洪蘊嘗以方藥謁見。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was at the Shu residence, Hongyun once presented himself with prescriptions and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenzong was still at his princely residence in Shu, Hongyun once visited him bearing prescriptions and medicines.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，補右街首座，累轉左街副僧錄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was appointed chief seat of the Right Avenue, and through successive transfers became deputy registrar of monks of the Left Avenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was appointed chief seat of the Right Avenue and was eventually promoted to deputy registrar of monks of the Left Avenue.

sentences.zh: 洪蘊尤工診切，每先歲時言人生死，無不應。

translations.literal: Hongyun was especially adept at pulse diagnosis; every year in advance he would speak of who would live or die, and without exception it came true.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyun was especially skilled at pulse diagnosis. Each year he would predict in advance who would live and who would die, and without fail his predictions came true.

sentences.zh: 湯劑精至，貴戚大臣有疾者，多詔遣診療。

translations.literal: His decoctions were exquisitely refined; when noble kin and great ministers fell ill, the court often ordered him dispatched to diagnose and treat.
translations.idiomatic: His medicinal decoctions were prepared with exceptional care, and when members of the imperial clan or senior ministers fell ill, the court frequently ordered him sent to diagnose and treat them.

sentences.zh: 景德元年卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Jingde, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jingde at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 又有廬山僧法堅，亦以善醫著名，久遊京師，嘗賜紫方袍，號廣濟大師，後還山。

translations.literal: Also Mount Lu monk Fajian was renowned for skill in medicine; he long traveled the capital, was once granted a purple square robe and the title Great Master Guangji, and later returned to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Mount Lu monk Fajian, who was likewise famous for his medical skill. He spent many years in the capital, was once granted a purple square robe and the title Great Master Guangji, and later returned to his mountain.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，以雍王元份久被疾，召赴闕，至則元份已薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, because Prince Yong Yuan Fen had long been afflicted with illness, he was summoned to court; upon arrival Yuan Fen had already died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde, Prince Yong Yuan Fen had long been gravely ill, and Fajian was summoned to court—but by the time he arrived, the prince was already dead.

sentences.zh: 法堅復歸山而卒。

translations.literal: Fajian again returned to the mountain and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fajian returned to his mountain and died there.

sentences.zh: 蘇澄隱字棲真，真定人。

translations.literal: Su Chengyin, courtesy name Qizhen, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chengyin, styled Qizhen, was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 為道士，住龍興觀，得養生之術，年八十餘不衰老。

translations.literal: He became a Daoist priest, resided at Longxing Abbey, obtained methods of nourishing life, and though over eighty years old did not age.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Daoist priest and lived at Longxing Abbey, where he mastered methods of nourishing life. Though past eighty, he showed no sign of age.

sentences.zh: 後唐明宗嘗下詔召之，又令宰相馮道致書諭旨，曆清泰、天福中繼有聘命，並辭疾不至。

translations.literal: Later Tang Mingzong once issued an edict summoning him, and also ordered chancellor Feng Dao to send a letter conveying the imperial intent; through Qingtai and Tianfu successive appointments came, but all were declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang Mingzong once issued an edict summoning him and had Chancellor Feng Dao write to convey the imperial wish. Appointments continued through the Qingtai and Tianfu eras, but Chengyin always declined on grounds of illness and never came.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹主兀欲立，求有名稱僧道加以恩命，惟澄隱不受。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler Wuyu established himself and sought renowned monks and Daoists to confer favors upon; only Chengyin did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun, when the Khitan ruler Wuyu took the throne, he sought out eminent monks and Daoists to honor with imperial favor. Chengyin alone refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 當時公卿自馮道、李崧、和凝而下，皆在鎮陽，日造其室與談宴，各賦詩以贈。

translations.literal: At that time the high officials from Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning downward were all at Zhenyang; daily they visited his chamber for conversation and feasts, each composing poems as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the leading officials, from Feng Dao, Li Song, and He Ning downward, were all at Zhenyang. They visited his dwelling daily for conversation and feasting, and each composed poems to present to him.

sentences.zh: 周廣順、顯德中，詔存問之。

translations.literal: During Later Zhou Guangshun and Xiande, edicts inquired after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun and Xiande eras of Later Zhou, the court sent edicts inquiring after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 太祖征太原還，駐蹕鎮陽，召見行宮，命中使掖升殿，謂之曰：「京師作建隆觀，思得有道之士居之，師累辭召命，豈懷土耶？」

translations.literal: When Taizu returned from the campaign against Taiyuan, he halted at Zhenyang, summoned him to the traveling palace, ordered an inner attendant to support him up to the hall, and said to him: "The capital is building Jianlong Abbey, and I wish to have a man of the Way dwell there; Master, you have repeatedly declined summons—is it because you are attached to your native soil?"
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu returned from his campaign against Taiyuan and halted at Zhenyang, he summoned Chengyin to his traveling palace and had a palace attendant help him up the steps to the hall. The emperor said to him, "We are building Jianlong Abbey in the capital and wish to install a man of the Way there. You have repeatedly declined our summons—is it because you are unwilling to leave your home?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大梁帝宅，浩穰繁會，非林泉之士所可寄跡也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Daliang is the imperial residence, vast, crowded, and thronged—it is not a place where one of forest and spring can lodge."
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin replied, "Daliang is the imperial capital—vast, crowded, and bustling. It is no place for one who dwells among forests and springs."

sentences.zh: 上察其意，亦不強之，賜茶百斤、絹二百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived his intent and did not compel him, granting a hundred jin of tea and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood his meaning and did not press him further. He granted him a hundred jin of tea and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又幸其觀，問曰：「師年逾八十而氣貌益壯，善養生者也。」

translations.literal: Again visiting his abbey, he asked: "Master, you are over eighty yet your vital spirit and appearance grow ever stronger—you are one who knows how to nourish life."
translations.idiomatic: On another visit to his abbey, the emperor asked, "Master, you are past eighty, yet your vital energy and bearing grow ever stronger. You must be skilled in the art of nourishing life."

sentences.zh: 因問其術，對曰：「臣之養生，不過精思練氣爾，帝王養生即異於是。

translations.literal: He then inquired about his method; he replied: "My nourishing of life is nothing more than refined meditation and breath cultivation—that of an emperor is different from this.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked about his method. Chengyin replied, "My way of nourishing life is nothing more than refined meditation and breath cultivation. The way an emperor nourishes life is quite different.

sentences.zh: 老子曰：『我無為而民自化，我無欲而民自正。』

translations.literal: Laozi says: 'When I do nothing, the people transform themselves; when I am without desire, the people rectify themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, 'When I do nothing, the people transform themselves; when I am without desire, the people set themselves right.'

sentences.zh: 無為無欲，凝神太和，昔黃帝、唐堯享國永年，得此道也。」

translations.literal: Without action and without desire, concentrating the spirit in great harmony—of old Huangdi and Tang Yao enjoyed the state for long years because they obtained this Way."
translations.idiomatic: Through nonaction and freedom from desire, concentrating the spirit in perfect harmony—this is how the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao ruled long and well. They attained this Way."

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賜紫衣一襲、銀器五百兩、帛五百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly rejoiced and granted one set of purple robes, five hundred liang of silver vessels, and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted him a set of purple robes, five hundred liang of silver vessels, and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 年僅百歲而卒。

translations.literal: He died at nearly a hundred years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at nearly one hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 丁少微，毫州真源人。

translations.literal: Ding Shaowei was a native of Zhenyuan in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shaowei was a native of Zhenyuan in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 為道士，持齋戒，奉科儀尤為精至。

translations.literal: He became a Daoist priest, observed fasting and precepts, and performed ritual protocols with especial refinement.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Daoist priest, kept strict fasts and precepts, and performed liturgical rites with exceptional precision.

sentences.zh: 嘗隱華山潼穀，密通陳摶所居，與摶齊名，少微誌尚清潔，摶嗜酒適性，其道不同，未嘗相往還。

translations.literal: He once secluded himself in Tong Valley on Mount Hua, which had a hidden path to where Chen Tuan dwelt; he was famous alongside Tuan, but Shaowei's aspiration was purity and integrity while Tuan loved wine and followed his nature—their paths differed and they never visited each other.
translations.idiomatic: He once lived in seclusion in Tong Valley on Mount Hua, which had a secret path to Chen Tuan's dwelling. He was as famous as Tuan, but Shaowei aspired to purity while Tuan loved wine and followed his own inclinations. Their ways differed, and they never visited one another.

sentences.zh: 少微善服氣，多餌藥，年百餘歲，康強無疾。

translations.literal: Shaowei was skilled at breath cultivation, frequently took medicinal elixirs, was over a hundred years old, vigorous and without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was skilled at breath cultivation and often took medicinal elixirs. He lived to be over a hundred, vigorous and free of illness.

sentences.zh: 始，卜居山上，起壇場淨室，通夕朝禮，五十餘年未嘗稍懈。

translations.literal: At the beginning, having chosen to dwell on the mountain, he erected ritual platforms and pure chambers, performing dawn worship through the night, and for over fifty years never slackened even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: From the start, having settled on the mountain, he built ritual platforms and pure chambers and performed dawn worship through the night. For more than fifty years he never slackened even slightly.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，召赴闕，以金丹、巨勝、南芝、玄芝為獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, he was summoned to court and presented gold elixir, giant mushrooms, southern fungus, and dark fungus.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was summoned to court and presented gold elixir, giant mushrooms, southern lingzhi, and dark lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 留數月，遣還山。

translations.literal: He stayed several months, then was sent back to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at court for several months before being sent back to his mountain.

sentences.zh: 七年冬卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 趙自然，太平繁昌人，家荻港旁，以鬻茗為業，本名王九。

translations.literal: Zhao Ziran was a native of Fanchang in Taiping; his family lived beside Digiang and made a living selling tea; his original name was Wang Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ziran was a native of Fanchang in Taiping. His family lived beside Digiang and made their living selling tea. His original name was Wang Jiu.

sentences.zh: 始十三，疾甚，父抱詣青華觀，許為道士。

translations.literal: When he was thirteen, he was gravely ill; his father carried him to Qinghua Abbey and pledged him as a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: When he was thirteen he fell gravely ill. His father carried him to Qinghua Abbey and pledged him to become a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 後夢一人狀貌魁偉，綸巾素袍，鬢髮班白，自雲姓陰，引之登高山，謂曰：「汝有道氣，吾將教汝辟穀之法。」

translations.literal: Later he dreamed of a man of imposing appearance, with silk headcloth and plain robe, temples and hair streaked with white, who said his surname was Yin, led him up a high mountain, and told him: "You have the breath of the Way; I shall teach you the method of grain abstinence."
translations.idiomatic: Later he dreamed of a man of imposing stature, wearing a silk headcloth and plain robe, his temples and hair streaked with white. The man said his surname was Yin, led him up a high mountain, and told him, "You possess the breath of the Way. I shall teach you the method of abstaining from grain."

sentences.zh: 乃出青柏枝令啖，夢中食之。

translations.literal: He then produced a green cypress branch and had him chew it; in the dream he ate it.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced a green cypress branch and had him chew it, and in the dream Ziran ate it.

sentences.zh: 及覺，遂不食，神氣清爽，每聞火食氣即嘔，惟生果清泉而已。

translations.literal: Upon waking he then did not eat; his spirit and vital energy were clear and refreshed; whenever he smelled cooked food he would vomit—only raw fruit and clear spring water.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he could no longer eat. His spirit was clear and refreshed, but the smell of cooked food made him vomit. He subsisted on raw fruit and clear spring water alone.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復夢向見老人教以篆書數百字，寤悉能記。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he again dreamed of the old man seen before teaching him several hundred characters in seal script; upon waking he could remember them all.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he dreamed again of the same old man, who taught him several hundred characters in seal script. When he awoke he could remember every one.

sentences.zh: 寫以示人，皆不能識。

translations.literal: He wrote them out to show people, and none could recognize them.
translations.idiomatic: He copied them out to show others, but no one could read them.

sentences.zh: 或云：「此非篆也，乃道家符籙耳。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "These are not seal script but Daoist talismans."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "These are not seal script at all—they are Daoist talismans."

sentences.zh: 嘗為《元道歌》，言修練之要。

translations.literal: He once composed "Song of the Primordial Way," speaking of the essentials of cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Song of the Primordial Way," setting forth the essentials of spiritual cultivation.

sentences.zh: 知州王洞表其事，太宗召赴闕，親問之，賜道士服，改名自然，賚錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Dong memorialized the matter; Taizong summoned him to court, questioned him in person, granted Daoist robes, changed his name to Ziran, and bestowed three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Dong memorialized his case to the throne. Taizong summoned him to court, questioned him in person, granted him Daoist robes, changed his name to Ziran, and bestowed three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 月餘遣還，住青華觀。

translations.literal: After slightly more than a month he was sent back to reside at Qinghua Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a month he was sent back to live at Qinghua Abbey.

sentences.zh: 後因病，飲食如故。

translations.literal: Later because of illness he ate food as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he fell ill, he resumed eating ordinary food.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，詔曰：「如聞自然頗精修養之術。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict said: "We have heard that Ziran is quite skilled in cultivation methods."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu an edict declared, "We have heard that Ziran is highly skilled in the arts of spiritual cultivation."

sentences.zh: 委發轉使楊覃訪其行跡，命內侍武永全召至闕下，屢得對，賜紫衣，改青華觀曰延禧。

translations.literal: It entrusted transit commissioner Yang Tan to investigate his conduct, ordered inner attendant Wu Yongquan to summon him to court, he had many audiences, was granted purple robes, and Qinghua Abbey was renamed Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court entrusted transit commissioner Yang Tan with investigating his conduct and ordered palace attendant Wu Yongquan to summon him to court. He had many audiences with the emperor, was granted purple robes, and Qinghua Abbey was renamed Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 自然以母老求還侍養，許之。

translations.literal: Ziran, because his mother was old, requested to return to serve and support her, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ziran asked to return home to care for his aged mother, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，又有鄭榮者，本禁軍，戌壁州還，夜遇神人謂曰：「汝有道氣，勿火食。」

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu there was also Zheng Rong, originally of the palace guard; returning from garrison duty at Bichou, at night he met a divine being who told him: "You have the breath of the Way—do not eat cooked food."
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu there was also Zheng Rong, formerly of the palace guard. Returning from garrison duty at Bichou, he encountered a divine being at night who told him, "You possess the breath of the Way. Do not eat cooked food."

sentences.zh: 因授以醫術救人。

translations.literal: He was thereby given medical skills to save people.
translations.idiomatic: The being then taught him medical arts with which to heal others.

sentences.zh: 七年，賜名自清，度為道士，居上清宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was granted the name Ziqing, ordained as a Daoist priest, and dwelt at Shangqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was granted the name Ziqing, ordained as a Daoist priest, and installed at Shangqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 所傳藥能愈大風疾，民多求之。

translations.literal: The medicine he transmitted could cure leprosy; the people frequently sought it.
translations.idiomatic: The medicine he dispensed could cure leprosy, and the people came to him in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 皆刺臂血和餅給焉。

translations.literal: He would prick his arm for blood, mix it with cakes, and give it to them.
translations.idiomatic: He would prick his own arm for blood, mix it into cakes, and give these to those who sought his aid.

sentences.zh: 又有秦州民家子趙抱一者，常牧羊田間。

translations.literal: Also there was Zhao Baoyi, a commoner's son from Qinzhou, who often herded sheep in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Baoyi, a commoner's son from Qinzhou, who often tended sheep in the fields.

sentences.zh: 一夕，有叩門召之者，以杖引行，杖端有氣如煙，其香可悅。

translations.literal: One evening someone knocked at the door and summoned him; with a staff he led him along—the staff's end had vapor like smoke, its fragrance pleasing.
translations.idiomatic: One evening someone knocked at his door and summoned him. The visitor led him along with a staff whose tip emitted fragrant vapor like smoke.

sentences.zh: 俄至山崖絕頂，見數人會飲，音樂交奏，與人間無異。

translations.literal: Soon they reached a cliff's sheer summit, where he saw several people feasting together, music interweaving—it was no different from the human world.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they reached the sheer summit of a cliff, where he saw several people feasting together to the sound of interwoven music—it was no different from life in the human world.

sentences.zh: 抱一駭而不測。

translations.literal: Baoyi was startled and could not fathom it.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi was terrified and could not comprehend what he saw.

sentences.zh: 會巡檢司過其下，聞樂聲，疑群盜歡聚，集村民梯崖而上。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the patrol office passed beneath; hearing the music, they suspected a band of robbers reveling together, gathered villagers, and climbed the cliff by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile a patrol detachment passed below, heard the music, and suspected a band of robbers carousing. They gathered villagers and climbed the cliff on ladders.

sentences.zh: 至則無所睹，抱一獨在，援以下之，具言其故。

translations.literal: Upon arriving they saw nothing; Baoyi alone was there—they pulled him down and he fully recounted the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the top they found nothing—Baoyi alone was there. They helped him down, and he told them the whole story.

sentences.zh: 凡經夕，若俄頃。

translations.literal: Though a whole night had passed, it seemed but a moment.
translations.idiomatic: A whole night had passed, yet to him it seemed but a moment.

sentences.zh: 自是不喜熟食，凡火化者未嘗曆口。

translations.literal: From then on he disliked cooked food; anything touched by fire never crossed his lips.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on he would not eat cooked food; nothing touched by fire ever passed his lips.

sentences.zh: 茹甘菊、柏葉、果實、井泉，間亦飲酒，貌如嬰兒。

translations.literal: He ate sweet chrysanthemum, cypress leaves, fruits, and wellspring water, occasionally also drank wine, and his appearance was like an infant's.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on sweet chrysanthemum, cypress leaves, fruit, and well water, occasionally drinking wine as well. His face looked like that of an infant.

sentences.zh: 素不習文墨，口占辭句，頗成篇詠。

translations.literal: He had never studied writing; composing verses orally, they formed complete poems.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had never studied letters, he could compose verses extemporaneously that formed complete poems.

sentences.zh: 有道家之趣。

translations.literal: He had the flavor of Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: There was something of the Daoist about him.

sentences.zh: 遂不親農事，野行露宿。

translations.literal: He then no longer engaged in farming, wandering in the wild and sleeping under the dew.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave up farming altogether, wandering the wilds and sleeping under the open sky.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，至京師，猶丱角，詔賜名，度為道士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he reached the capital, still wearing the topknot of youth; an edict granted him a name and ordained him as a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he came to the capital, still wearing the topknot of youth. An edict granted him a name and ordained him as a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 自是間歲或一至京師，常令居太一宮，與人言多養生事焉。

translations.literal: From then on every year or two he would once come to the capital; he was regularly ordered to reside at Taiyi Palace, and in conversing with people spoke mostly of matters of nourishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he visited the capital every year or two and was regularly assigned to reside at Taiyi Palace, where his conversations with others centered on the art of nourishing life.
